The robot body supports a head drill bit shaped as a cone. The head drill bit features a plurality of second rotating spiral blades wound on its surface for efficient soil penetration. Inlaid gears and hemispherical roller bits enhance drilling into varied soil densities. The head drill bit can retract and extend to adapt drilling force, minimizing damage while maximizing penetration speed.
[0029]  Surrounding the robot body are multi-directionally adjustable rotating blades. These are arranged in three groups of six blades total, encircling the body. Each blade comprises a cylindrical steel pipe with a series of first rotating spiral blades. By individually adjusting blade retraction via telescopic devices, the robot can pivot and steer in any direction, navigating around obstacles and moving along the steepest gas concentration gradient path.
[0030]  Omnidirectional Acquisition Module:
Placed strategically on the robot body , this module includes an image collector at the front end and multiple gas sensors distributed along the head and tail. The gas sensors are small, high-precision devices capable of detecting methane, natural gas, hydrogen, CO₂, and other target gases. Each sensor is protected by a blocking cover perforated with small openings that allow gas to pass while preventing soil ingress.
[0031]  The image collector may be an ultrasonic or optical sensor capturing forward-facing visuals. When combined with gas sensor data, these images help the intelligent control module distinguish pipeline surfaces, weld joints, or structural anomalies indicative of a leak zone.
[0032]  Power Module:
The power module comprises external power supply, built-in power cells inside the robot body, and a set of motors—at least a first motor inside the robot body and a second motor mounted on the multi-directionally adjustable rotating blades. The external power supply might be a DC source from above ground connected via a combined cable.
[0033]  The combined cable includes a power line, a signal line, and a guide rope. It establishes real-time communication, supplying steady power, and transmits sensor data and control signals between the robot and a ground-based control center. Such continuous connectivity ensures unlimited operational time and immediate remote supervision if needed.
[0034]  Intelligent Control Module & AI/ML Subsystem:
The intelligent control module incorporates:
• A control device responsible for executing navigation strategies, receiving sensor data, and issuing commands to motors and actuators.
• A signal receiver and transmitter for wireless or wired communication with surface operators, enabling remote monitoring and instruction updates.
• A GPS positioning device for tracking the robot’s real-time subterranean location (insofar as GPS or similar localization data can be approximated underground by auxiliary means, e.g., inertial navigation or RFID beacons near known reference points).
[0035]  The novel AI/ML subsystem constitutes a critical improvement over prior art. It includes a machine learning inference engine trained on historical leakage scenarios, soil density models, and pipeline layout patterns. The AI/ML models can be neural networks or advanced regression algorithms, continuously updating their internal parameters as new sensor data streams in. This adaptive learning allows the robot to refine its search pattern for more direct and quicker pathfinding to the leak location.
[0036]  AI/ML Control System Operation:
The AI/ML subsystem receives gas concentration data from multiple sensors, comparing differences between head and tail readings. If the concentration at the head surpasses that at the tail, the AI infers a forward direction is favorable. Conversely, if tail concentration dominates or no gradient emerges, it may instruct a turn via blade retraction on one side, guiding the robot toward a more promising direction.
[0037]  The AI also correlates image data with known pipeline geometries. By classifying image patterns and comparing them with stored templates or ML-trained recognition models, the subsystem can confirm proximity to pipeline segments or detect anomalies consistent with leaking joints or corrosion-induced openings.
[0038]  Over time, as the robot gathers more data, the AI refines its predictive models. For example, it may learn that certain soil types reduce the reliability of certain sensors or that certain gas concentration profiles are more indicative of leaks. Such learned intelligence enables more precise, context-sensitive navigation.
[0039]  Movement and Steering:
Under instructions from the AI/ML subsystem, the control device directs the motorized telescopic devices to extend or retract the multi-directional blades . By asymmetrically adjusting blade extension, the robot changes orientation. The head drill bit continues to rotate and advance forward, guided by these subtle adjustments.
[0040]  If gas concentration sensors detect a strong gradient in a specific radial direction, the AI instructs the telescopic devices on that side to retract slightly, pivoting the robot toward the gradient’s source. Simultaneously, if image analysis suggests the presence of pipeline materials, the AI will confirm that direction, refining the steering accordingly.
[0041]  Detecting and Localizing the Leak:
The goal is to find a location where gas concentration plateaus at a high value, and the image data suggests proximity to pipeline structures. At that point, the AI/ML logic concludes that the leak location is near, and the robot can stop drilling or mark the position.
[0042]  Using the GPS positioning device (or equivalent underground localization technique), the robot logs its current coordinates. These coordinates are sent back to the ground control center. Technicians then know exactly where to excavate with minimal guesswork. This reduces time, cost, and the risk of injury or environmental harm.
[0043]  Operation Flow Example:
• Step 1: The robot, placed on the ground above suspected pipeline areas, is activated and commences drilling downward.
• Step 2: As it penetrates the soil, gas sensors continuously measure concentrations, and the image collector scans the front area.
• Step 3: The AI/ML subsystem receives data every few seconds, computes concentration gradients, compares image patterns, and adjusts movement.
• Step 4: If concentration difference at the head is positive, the robot moves forward. If not, it pivots until a more favorable gradient emerges.
• Step 5: Once an image pattern consistent with a pipeline is recognized and gas concentration stabilizes at a high level, the AI judges the leak location to be found.
• Step 6: The position is recorded and transmitted to surface operators, who can excavate precisely at that spot.
[0044]  Construction Materials and Durability:
The robot’s external shell and drill bits use hardened steel or other robust alloys for durability. The blade assemblies and telescopic devices are sealed to prevent soil infiltration. Gas sensors have protective layers and blocking covers that filter debris and ensure reliable measurements.
[0045]  Sensor Calibration and Upgrades:
The AI/ML subsystem can integrate calibration routines. Initially, the robot might run baseline tests to align sensor readings. Over missions, the machine learning models update calibration parameters, improving accuracy in diverse soil conditions and gas compositions.
[0046]   Power Considerations:
Continuous DC power supplied through the combined cable (5) allows long-duration missions. Internal batteries may serve as backups if external power is interrupted. The AI/ML subsystem’s computations are optimized for low power consumption, possibly employing on-chip accelerators for ML inference.
[0047]  Communications and Data Security:
Secure protocols ensure data from the robot’s sensors and camera remain untampered. Encryption methods may be used to protect sensitive pipeline location data. The AI/ML models can also be updated over secure channels, improving intelligence over time.
[0048]  Comparisons to Prior Art:
Conventional robots lack the sophisticated AI/ML-driven navigation and do not combine gas gradient analysis with image-based recognition. This invention’s novelty lies in using machine learning to dynamically interpret sensor data, predict optimal paths, and refine drilling and steering strategies. Such capabilities were not obvious to skilled artisans relying on static heuristics or manual operator guidance.
[0049]  Versatility and Scalability:
While described for gas pipelines, the robot’s design and AI/ML control framework can adapt to other buried utilities, such as water or sewage pipelines. By adjusting sensor types and ML training data, the system can locate leaks in various underground infrastructures.
[0050]  Manufacturing and Maintenance:
Standard machining processes fabricate the drilling and blade components. The sensors and electronics, including AI/ML chips, are integrated on-board. Maintenance involves checking blade integrity, sensor cleanliness, and software model updates for the AI/ML subsystem.
[0051]  Regulatory and Safety Considerations:
Faster leak localization reduces environmental hazards and aligns with safety regulations. By minimizing unnecessary excavations, the robot also lessens ecological disturbances.
[0052]  In essence, the disclosed invention delivers a unique combination of mechanical drilling prowess and cutting-edge AI-driven intelligence to tackle a longstanding industrial challenge. The synergy of advanced sensing, ML-based decision-making, and robust hardware ensures high reliability and swift leak localization.
[0053]  Although some adaptation may be necessary for specific pipeline depths, soil conditions, or gas types, the general principles remain intact: the robot’s AI model learns from ongoing operations, continuously improving its ability to discern and follow gas concentration gradients and pipeline imagery.
[0054]  Enhanced reliability arises from the system’s ability to cross-check gas sensor signals with visual cues. If gas readings alone prove ambiguous in certain soils, image data can confirm proximity to pipeline surfaces. The AI logic fuses these modalities, robustly guiding the robot even in complex or unfamiliar underground environments.
[0055]  Given the generality and adaptability of the AI subsystem, future upgrades might incorporate advanced deep learning models, more sophisticated pattern recognition for pipeline anomalies, or predictive maintenance to warn operators of impending sensor failures. The invention thus forms a platform for continuous improvement.

Abstract:

The present invention discloses a system and method for simultaneously producing high-purity liquid nitrogen and high-purity liquid carbon dioxide from flue gas at low cost. The system integrates a flue gas pressurization and cooling subsystem, a CO₂/N₂ front-end separation subsystem utilizing pressure swing adsorption, a liquid CO₂ preparation subsystem, and a high-purity liquid N₂ preparation subsystem. Crucially, the invention incorporates an AI-integrated predictive control system that employs real-time sensor data and machine learning algorithms to dynamically optimize process parameters, enhance energy efficiency, maintain product purity, and perform predictive maintenance. By leveraging compression heat from CO₂ boosters to assist PSA regeneration and using N₂ liquefier-derived cooling capacity to condense CO₂, the system achieves efficient resource utilization. The AI-driven framework allows adaptation to varying feed compositions, external economic factors, and equipment conditions, offering substantial improvements in energy consumption, operational stability, and economic performance compared to conventional, static approaches.

Description:
[0001]   The present invention relates generally to the field of environmental protection, particularly to systems and methods for recovering and purifying industrial gases. More specifically, it provides a system and method for simultaneously producing high-purity liquid nitrogen and high-purity liquid carbon dioxide from flue gas streams at low cost, integrated with an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) predictive control and optimization platform.
[0002]   As such, the invention sits at the intersection of chemical process engineering, cryogenic separation technology, pressure swing adsorption (PSA)-based gas purification, and AI-driven intelligent process control.
BACKGROUND 
[0003]   Reducing carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions is critical to mitigating climate change. Industrial processes, such as steelmaking and coal-based power generation, produce large volumes of flue gas, containing CO₂, nitrogen (N₂), oxygen (O₂), water vapor, and trace impurities. Typically, flue gas after standard treatments (desulfurization, denitrification, dust removal) still comprises about 10-20% CO₂ and more than 70% N₂.
[0004]   Technologies for CO₂ capture and separation from flue gas include chemical absorption, membrane separation, and pressure swing adsorption (PSA). However, conventional approaches often suffer from high energy consumption and complex regeneration needs, particularly for low-concentration CO₂ streams.
[0005]   Concurrently, nitrogen is widely used across multiple industries, often requiring ultra-high purity (≥99.999%). Conventional air separation units (ASUs) consume substantial energy to produce high-purity nitrogen. With flue gas containing a large fraction of N₂ (especially after partial CO₂ removal), it becomes attractive to recover and purify that nitrogen, reducing reliance on expensive ASUs.
[0006]   Prior art solutions have addressed CO₂ capture using PSA and have attempted to reclaim nitrogen from flue gas. However, many of these approaches still incur high energy costs and are limited to gaseous nitrogen outputs, restricting downstream applications. Additionally, conventional control systems are typically static, employing fixed setpoints and manual adjustments, not optimized for dynamic conditions or market-driven parameters.
[0007]   There is thus a pressing need for an integrated system that can: (1) efficiently capture and liquefy CO₂ at high purity, (2) purify and liquefy nitrogen at very high purity, (3) leverage synergy between PSA and cryogenic operations, and (4) dynamically optimize operation via AI-based predictive control, reducing energy consumption, responding to varying input and demand conditions, and providing predictive maintenance capabilities.
[0008]   Introducing artificial intelligence into the control and operation of such a system enables continuous adaptation to changing feed compositions, fluctuating energy prices, and product demand variations. AI-driven predictive control and optimization allow for sophisticated decision-making that goes beyond conventional PID loops or operator-driven adjustments.
[0009]   By integrating AI models that learn from historical data, current sensor inputs, and external economic signals, the system can smartly modulate process parameters. This ensures maximum overall efficiency, minimal environmental impact, and potentially significant cost savings.
[0010]   No known prior art integrates advanced AI predictive control with a combined PSA and cryogenic system producing both high-purity liquid CO₂ and liquid N₂ from flue gas. The invention herein fills this gap.
SUMMARY 
[0011]   In view of the above issues, the present invention provides a system and method for simultaneously producing high-purity liquid nitrogen and high-purity liquid carbon dioxide at low cost by utilizing flue gas, combined with an AI-integrated predictive control system.
[0012]   The system includes four main subsystems: (1) a flue gas pressurization and cooling subsystem that cleans, cools, and conditions raw flue gas; (2) a CO₂/N₂ front-end separation subsystem employing PSA technology to capture CO₂ and produce a N₂-rich tail gas; (3) a liquid CO₂ preparation subsystem to purify, cool, and liquefy CO₂; and (4) a high-purity liquid N₂ preparation subsystem that purifies, liquefies, and recovers nitrogen from the PSA tail gas.
[0013]   Crucially, the invention introduces an AI-integrated predictive control platform. This platform gathers real-time operational data—temperature, pressures, impurity concentrations, flow rates—and external factors such as electricity costs or desired production rates. A machine learning model continuously refines a predictive process model, guiding adjustments of PSA cycle timing, compressor speeds, refrigerant flows, and distillation column parameters.
[0014]   By employing an AI-driven supervisory control, the system can dynamically optimize regeneration energy consumption, select optimal operating conditions, and achieve desired purity and liquefaction efficiency. The AI module can also detect early signs of equipment wear or adsorbent degradation, triggering predictive maintenance and minimizing unscheduled downtime.
[0015]   The invention leverages the compression heat from CO₂ boosters to assist PSA regeneration and the cooling capacity from the N₂ liquefaction subsystem to help condense CO₂, thus integrating energy streams efficiently. Additionally, the dry exhaust gas from the N₂ preparation system can be utilized to recover cold energy from the flue gas cooling tower.
[0016]   By harnessing AI, the system can respond to fluctuating feed composition and external conditions, thereby maintaining consistent product purity and throughput. The result is a more stable, efficient, and economically attractive solution for industries that generate flue gas and need stable supplies of high-purity N₂ and CO₂.
[0017]   Therefore, the invention solves the issues of high energy consumption in low-concentration CO₂ capture, provides a valuable resource in liquid nitrogen, and reduces complexity by introducing a robust AI-based decision-support and optimization mechanism.
[0018]   In sum, the invention provides a highly integrated and intelligent solution, blending PSA, cryogenic separation, and advanced AI predictive control. The resultant capabilities surpass those of conventional fixed-setpoint systems and represent a significant advancement in environmental technology.
[0019]   The invention has broad applicability in power generation, steelmaking, coal chemical industries, and other sectors producing large volumes of flue gas. It also aligns with global efforts to reduce carbon footprints and improve resource utilization.
[0020]   Taken together, the proposed system and method offer significant technical, economic, and environmental advantages.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWING
[0021]   FIG. 1 is a process flow diagram illustrating the general architecture of the integrated system, including the flue gas pressurization and cooling subsystem, the CO₂/N₂ front-end separation subsystem, the liquid CO₂ preparation subsystem, and the high-purity liquid N₂ preparation subsystem.
[0022]   The flowchart depicts the detailed workflow of the system for simultaneously producing high-purity liquid nitrogen (N₂) and liquid carbon dioxide (CO₂) from flue gas, integrated with AI-driven predictive control for dynamic optimization and efficiency.
[0023]   The process begins with flue gas entry, where raw flue gas is introduced into the Flue Gas Pressurization and Cooling Subsystem. This subsystem compresses the flue gas to the required pressure (0.5-0.8 MPa) and cools it to remove moisture and soluble impurities. It employs multiple cooling stages, including a cooling tower and water circulation system, to optimize energy usage.
[0024]   The conditioned flue gas is then directed to the CO₂/N₂ Front-End Separation Subsystem, which uses Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) technology to separate carbon dioxide from nitrogen-rich tail gas. The PSA towers adsorb CO₂ while allowing nitrogen and other gases to pass through. Once the adsorbent saturates, a vacuum pump desorbs the CO₂, which is collected in a buffer device. Simultaneously, the nitrogen-rich tail gas exits as a secondary stream.
[0025]   The CO₂-rich stream undergoes further processing in the Liquid CO₂ Preparation System. This system compresses the CO₂ using a booster, cools it through a series of refrigeration loops, and purifies it in a CO₂ purification tower. Final liquefaction occurs via a CO₂ condenser, producing high-purity liquid CO₂ (≥99.9%) as the final output.
[0026]   On the other hand, the nitrogen-rich tail gas flows into the High-Purity Liquid N₂ Preparation System. This subsystem involves a nitrogen liquefier and a low-temperature separation system, where the nitrogen is purified and liquefied. Gaseous nitrogen is separated, recycled, and reheated to enhance energy efficiency, while high-purity liquid nitrogen (≥99.999%) is drawn off as the final product. 
[0027]   The integration of these subsystems is managed by an AI-Integrated Predictive Control System, represented in the flowchart by multiple AI control modules.
[0028]   The AI system continuously monitors sensor inputs, including temperature, pressure, and gas composition. Using real-time data, the AI optimizes key parameters such as PSA cycle times, compressor speeds, and refrigeration flows. For the CO₂ processing pathway, the AI ensures efficient regeneration of adsorbents, maximizes CO₂ purity, and minimizes energy use. For the N₂ pathway, the AI refines liquefaction conditions to maintain ultra-high purity and optimal throughput.
[0029]   The AI also manages real-time system optimization, ensuring seamless operation under varying feed compositions, ambient conditions, and production demands. It incorporates predictive maintenance capabilities, analyzing sensor patterns to detect early signs of wear or degradation in components like adsorbents, compressors, or valves. By recommending timely maintenance, the AI minimizes downtime and extends system longevity.
[0030]   Additionally, the AI evaluates cost and energy efficiency adjustments, factoring in external variables such as electricity prices and carbon credit values. This allows the system to switch priorities, such as focusing more on N₂ or CO₂ production based on economic conditions, and leverage off-peak energy for cost savings.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION 
[0031]   The following detailed description is presented in terms of embodiments and examples, and should not be considered limiting. The invention may be practiced with various modifications and adaptations, as understood by those skilled in the art, within the scope of the appended claims.
[0032]   The invention contemplates a comprehensive solution for simultaneously producing high-purity liquid nitrogen and high-purity liquid carbon dioxide using flue gas. It integrates PSA for CO₂ capture, cryogenic processes for N₂ liquefaction, and an AI predictive control system for adaptive, optimized operation.
[0033]   The Flue Gas Pressurization and Cooling System: This subsystem includes a flue gas booster (1), a flue gas cooling tower (2), a water-cooling tower (3), a low-temperature water pump (4), and a chiller (5). Raw flue gas is compressed to 0.5-0.8 MPa and cooled, removing moisture and soluble impurities. The flue gas cooling tower may be divided into segments where normal temperature water is used in the lower section, and chilled water plus dry nitrogen in the upper section.
[0034]   Water circulating among these towers is intelligently managed. Normal temperature water enters via a first water valve (6), passes through a water cooling tower (3) to reduce energy consumption, and low-temperature water is introduced via a third water valve (8) and low-temperature water pump (4). When the N₂ system is offline, a fourth water valve (9) recirculates low-temperature water to maintain adequate cooling.
[0035]  CO₂/N₂ Front-End Separation System: The heart of the CO₂ capture is a plurality of PSA towers connected to the cooled flue gas through a first gas valve. PSA towers adsorb CO₂ and allow N₂ to pass. Once adsorbents saturate, vacuum pump desorbs CO₂-rich gas into a CO₂ buffer device. Non-adsorbed gases are sent to an adsorption tail gas buffer device.
[0036]   The CO₂ concentration in the desorbed stream can reach above 95%. To enhance desorption, hot fluid from a CO₂ booster is passed through the PSA towers, using compression heat for regeneration. This synergy lowers energy usage and increases CO₂ purity.
[0037]  Liquid CO₂ Preparation System: The CO₂ buffer device feeds CO₂ gas through a third gas valve into the CO₂ booster, raising pressure and temperature. This hot fluid assists PSA regeneration, then returns cooled fluid to a CO₂ evaporator, a CO₂ recooler, and a CO₂ purification tower.
[0038]   Within the CO₂ preparation system, a CO₂ condenser and an external refrigerant cycle (with refrigerant compressor, cooler, regenerator, and throttle valve) provide the necessary refrigeration to liquefy CO₂. The final CO₂ product, with purity exceeding 99.9%, exits as liquid CO₂ from the bottom of the CO₂ evaporator.
[0039]   If higher-grade, such as food-grade CO₂, is required, subsequent refining stages can be added to remove additional impurities.
[0040]  High-Purity Liquid Nitrogen Preparation System: Adsorption tail gas (rich in N₂, ~90%) from buffer device and gas from the CO₂ recooler outlet join via a sixth gas valve and enter a blower. This mixture is fed into a nitrogen liquefier through a seventh gas valve and cooled.
[0041]   Downstream, a low-temperature separation system purifies and liquefies the N₂. High-purity N₂ (≥99.999%) is obtained and may be drawn off as a supercooled liquid product. Part of the cryogenic fluid is diverted from the nitrogen liquefier to the CO₂ recooler, serving as a cold source for CO₂ condensation, thereby integrating both systems energetically.
[0042]   The nitrogen liquefier, gas-liquid separator, nitrogen booster, nitrogen cooler, and expansion cooling system collaborate to achieve efficient liquefaction. High-pressure, low-temperature streams feed the gas-liquid separator, yielding liquid N₂ at the bottom and sending gaseous N₂ back for reheating and recycling.
[0043]   Exhaust gas from the low-temperature separation system is reheated by the nitrogen liquefier and directed to the water cooling tower, recovering cold energy to further lower flue gas cooling requirements.
[0044]   AI-Integrated Predictive Control System: The invention incorporates an AI module that continuously monitors sensor data from across the system: temperatures, pressures, concentrations, flow rates, and mechanical vibration signatures. This module, uses machine learning to build predictive models correlating input conditions with desired outputs (purity, yield, energy usage).
[0045]   The AI module employs historical data and reinforcement learning algorithms. It predicts how changes in PSA cycle times, compressor speeds, tower pressures, and refrigerant flows affect system performance. Based on these predictions, it recommends real-time parameter adjustments, ensuring optimal CO₂ capture, N₂ purity, and minimal energy consumption.
[0046]   This AI system can also integrate external factors such as electricity pricing or carbon credit values. By factoring in economic conditions, the AI can recommend when to operate at partial load, switch priorities between N₂ and CO₂ production, or utilize off-peak energy to reduce operating costs.
[0047]   Another critical function of the AI is predictive maintenance. By analyzing patterns in sensor data—e.g., slight increases in pressure drop across adsorbers or subtle temperature drift in compressors—the AI identifies early signs of fouling, adsorbent degradation, or mechanical wear. It then suggests maintenance intervals, reducing downtime and preventing unplanned outages.
[0048]   The AI module interfaces with a supervisory control system that executes parameter changes through actuators (e.g., adjusting valve positions, changing compressor setpoints, or varying PSA cycle durations). Operators can oversee and override these decisions via a human-machine interface (HMI), ensuring transparency and safety.
[0049]   Suppose the flue gas composition shifts to slightly higher CO₂ concentration due to upstream feedstock changes. The AI detects increasing CO₂ loading in PSA towers and predicts that slight adjustments to PSA cycle timing and regeneration conditions could maintain stable CO₂ purity at minimal extra energy cost.
[0050]   Simultaneously, if electricity prices spike, the AI may recommend reducing compressor power at certain times or shifting production priorities. If the cryogenic subsystem’s load changes, the AI can adjust the fraction of cold source diverted from N₂ liquefier to CO₂ recooler to maintain optimal liquefaction efficiency.
[0051]   Over weeks of operation, the AI refines its model. If it observes that adsorbent performance declines subtly, it might schedule a maintenance alert before a significant performance drop occurs. Thus, not only day-to-day optimization is achieved, but also long-term reliability improvement.
[0052]   Integration with Distillation and Additional Refinements: The N₂ purification may involve one or more distillation towers in the low-temperature separation system. The AI can optimize reflux ratios, column pressures, and condenser duty to achieve target N₂ purity with minimal energy use. Similarly, for the CO₂ purification, the AI can adjust refrigerant cycle parameters to maintain stable CO₂ condensation at varying loads.
[0053]   External Refrigerant Cycle: The refrigerant loop for CO₂ condenser cooling is also under AI supervision. The AI chooses optimal compressor loading and throttling conditions to match real-time cooling demands, preventing unnecessary energy wastage.
[0054]   Equipment Selection and Customization: Flue gas booster selection (e.g., multi-stage centrifugal compressor) and valve sizing can be adapted to specific industrial contexts. The AI model can be retrained for different flue gas compositions or for different scales of production.
[0055]   Scalability: The system scales to large industrial plants or smaller pilot facilities. As data accumulates, the AI model grows more accurate, allowing scalable, site-specific optimization strategies.
[0056]   Environmental and Economic Impact: By recovering CO₂ from flue gas, the invention reduces greenhouse gas emissions. By producing high-purity liquid N₂ directly from flue gas, it avoids the energy-intensive steps of standard air separation. AI-driven efficiency gains translate into lower operational costs, improved competitiveness, and more sustainable industrial operations.
[0057]   Commissioning and Start-Up: Initially, operators may run the system in a semi-automatic mode, allowing the AI model to gather baseline data. After a learning period, the AI takes on a more autonomous role, incrementally refining control actions while maintaining operator oversight.
[0058]   Safety and Redundancy: Should sensors fail or the AI module become unavailable, the system can revert to predefined fallback modes with conservative setpoints. This ensures safety and continuity of production.
[0059]   Network Connectivity: The AI module may receive updates and improved models from a central server. Secure communication protocols ensure data integrity and protect against cyber threats. Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention pertains to pharmaceutical formulations and targeted drug delivery systems. Specifically, it focuses on coffee oil-based nanoparticles designed for the delivery of betamethasone sodium phosphate in the treatment of duodenal ulcers, ensuring sustained release, enhanced bioavailability, and minimized side effects.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Duodenal ulcers are a prevalent gastrointestinal disorder characterized by the erosion of the duodenal lining due to excessive stomach acid or other factors such as Helicobacter pylori infections. Current treatments involve antacids, proton pump inhibitors, and anti-inflammatory agents, which, while effective, suffer from limited bioavailability, potential side effects, and the need for frequent dosing.
Betamethasone sodium phosphate, a potent anti-inflammatory corticosteroid, has shown promise in reducing inflammation and promoting healing in ulcerative conditions. However, its application is limited by poor bioavailability and rapid degradation in the gastrointestinal tract. Traditional delivery methods fail to ensure its sustained release and targeted delivery to the duodenum.
The development of coffee oil-based nanoparticles offers a novel solution to these challenges. The use of coffee oil as a matrix enhances the stability and bioavailability of betamethasone sodium phosphate, while the nanoparticle design enables controlled release and targeted delivery to the duodenum. This innovative approach improves therapeutic efficacy, reduces dosing frequency, and minimizes systemic side effects.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The invention introduces coffee oil-based nanoparticles as a targeted drug delivery system for betamethasone sodium phosphate in the treatment of duodenal ulcers. These nanoparticles are formulated using the solvent emulsion-evaporation method, incorporating coffee oil as the matrix and stabilizing agents such as poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA).
The nanoparticles are spherical, with an average size of 150 nm, ensuring efficient absorption by the duodenal epithelium. They exhibit a drug loading efficiency of 68% and a sustained release profile over 24 hours. The enteric-coated formulation protects the nanoparticles from stomach acidity, ensuring their release at the target site.
Clinical applications of these nanoparticles include treating duodenal ulcers, reducing inflammation, and promoting healing. Additionally, the nanoparticles’ design supports combination therapies by encapsulating multiple therapeutic agents. This versatile and personalized approach offers significant advancements in gastrointestinal drug delivery.
 
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The Coffee Oil-Based Nanoparticles for Targeted Drug Delivery are formulated to optimize the therapeutic effects of betamethasone sodium phosphate in treating duodenal ulcers. The formulation involves the solvent emulsion-evaporation method, which ensures uniform nanoparticle size and drug encapsulation.
Initially, betamethasone sodium phosphate is dissolved in coffee oil, forming the oil phase, while PLGA and stabilizers such as polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) constitute the aqueous phase. The oil phase is emulsified into the aqueous phase under vigorous mixing, creating a stable emulsion. Solvent evaporation solidifies the polymer, forming spherical nanoparticles encapsulating the drug within the coffee oil matrix.
The resulting nanoparticles are characterized for size, morphology, and drug loading efficiency using techniques like dynamic light scattering (DLS) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The average size of 150 nm ensures efficient absorption by the intestinal epithelium, while the sustained release properties maintain therapeutic drug levels in the duodenum for prolonged periods.
The nanoparticles are incorporated into enteric-coated capsules or tablets to protect them from the acidic gastric environment. Upon reaching the duodenum, the enteric coating dissolves, releasing the nanoparticles for targeted action. The controlled release profile ensures consistent delivery of betamethasone sodium phosphate, reducing inflammation and promoting ulcer healing.
Field studies demonstrate the efficacy of these nanoparticles in significantly reducing ulcer indices and improving duodenal healing compared to conventional treatments. Their versatility allows for future modifications, including surface targeting agents or combination therapies, enhancing their application in personalized medicine and gastrointestinal care.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to nanotechnology and targeted drug delivery systems. Specifically, it focuses on the synthesis of doped ferrite nanoparticles using the Exploding Wire Technique (EWT) for magnetic drug delivery applications in cancer therapy, ensuring precise drug targeting, reduced side effects, and enhanced therapeutic efficacy.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide, with approximately 10 million deaths reported in 2020. Current therapeutic approaches, including chemotherapy and radiation, often cause significant side effects due to the non-specific targeting of healthy tissues. Recent advancements in nanoscience have revolutionized drug delivery systems, enabling targeted therapeutic interventions through multifunctional nanomaterials.
Iron oxide-based nanoparticles have emerged as promising candidates for cancer theragnostics due to their biocompatibility, magnetic properties, and ease of functionalization. However, conventional synthesis methods, such as hydrothermal and sol-gel processes, often face challenges like toxicity, environmental concerns, and limited scalability.
This invention introduces a novel approach using the Exploding Wire Technique (EWT) to synthesize doped ferrite nanoparticles. This method ensures precise control over size, stoichiometry, and magnetic properties, making the nanoparticles suitable for targeted drug delivery. By leveraging magnetic fields, the nanoparticles can deliver drugs to tumor sites with minimal impact on healthy tissues, offering a significant improvement over traditional cancer treatments.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The invention provides a nanoparticle-based magnetic drug delivery system specifically designed for targeted cancer therapy. Ferrite nanoparticles doped with transition metals are synthesized using the Exploding Wire Technique (EWT), ensuring uniform size distribution, non-toxicity, and optimized magnetic properties.
These nanoparticles are functionalized with biocompatible polymers to enhance drug loading capacity and stability. Upon administration, the nanoparticles are guided to tumor sites using an external magnetic field. Once localized, the drug is released in response to stimuli such as pH changes or redox reactions, ensuring precise delivery and reduced systemic toxicity.
The system's key features include controllable synthesis parameters, high drug loading efficiency, and tunable magnetic and dielectric properties. Field tests demonstrate the system's ability to improve therapeutic outcomes by enhancing drug concentration at tumor sites while minimizing side effects on healthy tissues.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The Nanoparticle-Based Magnetic Drug Delivery System leverages the Exploding Wire Technique (EWT) for the synthesis of doped ferrite nanoparticles. The EWT method involves passing a high-energy current through a metallic wire in a controlled environment, resulting in the formation of nanoparticles with precise size and stoichiometry.
The nanoparticles are doped with transition metals such as Cu, Zn, and Co to enhance their magnetic and dielectric properties. These properties enable efficient drug loading and magnetic guidance. The nanoparticles are further functionalized with biocompatible polymers, such as polyethylene glycol (PEG), to improve their stability, dispersibility, and compatibility with biological systems.
The drug delivery mechanism relies on the nanoparticles' ability to respond to external magnetic fields and localized stimuli. After systemic administration, the nanoparticles are guided to the tumor site using an alternating magnetic field. At the target site, the drug is released in response to stimuli such as pH variations in the tumor microenvironment or redox reactions. This controlled release minimizes off-target effects and enhances therapeutic efficacy.
Field tests demonstrate the system's effectiveness in targeting solid tumors, with significant reductions in tumor size and minimal side effects on healthy tissues. The scalability and eco-friendliness of the EWT synthesis method further establish the invention as a practical solution for advanced cancer therapy.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to a snow removal device for solar panel that automatically removes snow deposited over a solar panel by detecting the presence of snow and also eliminates the moisture from the solar panel in an automated manner.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002]  Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity, making them essential for renewable energy generation. However, the deposition of snow on solar panels obstruct sunlight, reducing energy output or halting it entirely. Snow accumulation creates a barrier, preventing efficient power generation. Additionally, if snow melts and moisture remains on the panel's surface, it leads to water seepage into electrical components, causing corrosion, electrical malfunctions, and potential damage over time. Removing snow and moisture is crucial to maintaining optimal panel performance, maximizing energy efficiency, and extending the lifespan of the panel by preventing long-term damage.

[0003]  Traditionally, people remove snow from solar panels using tools like soft brooms, roof rakes, or squeegees with long handles to gently clear the snow without damaging the panel's surface. Some people use heated cables placed around the edges of panels to melt snow. While these traditional methods are effective to some extent but they also pose several challenges and drawbacks. Manual removal is time-consuming and may involve climbing onto roofs or using ladders, posing risks of slips or falls. These methods also often fail to fully remove moisture, which lead to further issues.

The solar panel dust and snow remover is applicable to all solar systems, and can ensure the light transmission of solar panel glass; the installation is convenient, and the structure is simple; the flexibility is higher, the repair is simple and various environments can be adapted to; the snow and dust removing effects are significant, and the solar panel is not damaged in any way; and the service life is long. Though, CN’308 discloses about an invention that relates to a solar panel dust and snow remover. However, the cited invention lacks in removing the snow from the solar panel in an automated manner by detecting the presence of snow.

[0005] CN112491351A discloses about a solar panel dust removal and snow removal device.The solar panel dust removal and snow removal device comprises a solar panel, moving mechanisms, a connecting piece, a cleaning mechanism, a cable, a heat storage device, a conversion device and a connecting pipe, the moving mechanisms are arranged on the left side and the right side of the solar panel and drive the cleaning mechanism to move to clean the solar panel, and the connecting piece is fixedly connected to the bottom end of the rear end of the solar panel; a cleaning mechanism is arranged at the front end of the solar panel and used for cleaning accumulated snow in a dust box on the surface of the solar panel, the left side and the right side of the cleaning mechanism are fixedly connected with the moving mechanisms, the bottom end of the connecting piece is fixedly connected with the connecting pipe, the other end of the connecting pipe is fixedly connected with the heat storage device, the bottom end of the heat storage device is fixedly connected with the conversion device, cables are fixedly connected to the two sides of the conversion device, the other ends of the cables are fixedly connected with the bottom ends of the moving mechanisms, and the problem that dust and accumulated snow on the surface of the solar panel are inconvenient to clean is solved. Additionally, these existing devices also lacks in detecting and removing the presence of moisture over the solar panel in an automated manner.

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of removing snow from the surface of a solar panel in a self-sufficient manner by detecting the presence of snow deposited over the solar panel. In addition, the developed device also detects the presence of moisture over the solar panel and accordingly dry out the solar panel in an automated manner for preventing damage caused by moisture accumulation.

[0009]  An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of removing snow from a solar panel in an automated manner by detecting the presence of snow, thereby reducing manual efforts and consumption of time in the overall process.

[0021] The present invention relates to a snow removal device for solar panel that is capable of providing a means for removal of snow from a solar panel in an automated manner by detecting the presence of snow over the solar panel. Additionally, the proposed device is capable of detecting and removing the presence of moisture over the solar panel in an automated manner.

[0022]  Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of a snow removal device for solar panel is illustrated, comprising a rectangular frame 101, a sliding unit 102 installed along opposite edges of the frame 101, an elongated rod 103 is installed between the sliding units 102, plurality of telescopic links 104 incorporated downwardly on rod 103, a rectangular plate 105 is attached at the ends of each link by means of hinges 106, an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 107 installed on the frame 101, plurality of hot air blowers 108 installed along the frame 101, a microphone 109 provided on the frame 101, and plurality of LEDs 110 (light emitting diodes) mounted on the frame 101.

[0023]  The device disclosed herein comprises of a rectangular frame 101 incorporating various components associated with the device and developed to be positioned around periphery of a solar panel manually by a user. The frame 101 serves as the core structure and is made from strong, waterproof and lightweight materials which includes but not limited to hardened steel, aluminum alloy, hard fiber, and composite materials. These materials offer strength and rigidity to the frame 101 making it resistant to mechanical stress and pressure. The surface of the frame 101 is coated with material like Teflon or other low-friction coatings to improve wear resistance and reduce friction.

[0024]  Upon positioning the frame 101 around the periphery of the solar panel, the user is required to access a microphone 109 provided on the frame 101 to provide audio command regarding removing snow from the solar panel. The microphone 109 receives the user voice commands and converts the sound energy emitted by the user into electrical energy. Inside the microphone 109, a diaphragm made of plastic is present that moves back and forth when the sound wave hits the diaphragm, which then moves a coil attached to the diaphragm in the same way in order to generate an electrical signal proportional to the sound. The electric signal from coil flows to an amplifier which amplifies the electrical signal. The amplified electrical signal is then sent to an inbuilt microcontroller linked to the microphone 109.

[0025]  Upon receiving and processing the signal from the microphone 109, the microcontroller recognizes the user input voice command and accordingly generates a command to actuate an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 107 installed on the frame 101 and paired with a processor for capturing and processing multiple images in vicinity of the frame 101. The artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 107 comprises of a high-resolution camera lens, digital camera sensor and a processor, wherein the lens captures multiple images from different angles and perspectives in vicinity of the frame 101 with the help of digital camera sensor for providing comprehensive coverage of the solar panel.

[0026]  The captured images then go through pre-processing steps by the processor integrated with the camera. The processor carries out a sequence of image processing operation including pre-processing, feature extraction and classification in order to enhance the image quality, which includes adjusting brightness and contrast and removing any distortion or noise. The pre-processed images are transmitted to the microcontroller linked with the processor in the form of electrical signals.

[0027]  The microcontroller further processes the received signals in order to determine snow collected on the solar panel. A sliding unit 102 is installed along opposite edges of the frame 101 and having an elongated rod 103 installed between the sliding unit 102, wherein upon successful detection of snow on the solar panel, the microcontroller actuates the sliding unit 102 to translate the rod 103. The sliding unit 102 used herein consists of a sliding-rail and multiple rolling members which are integrated with a step motor. On actuation, the step motor rotates the rolling members in order to provide rolling motion to the members which results in sliding of the units for translating the rod 103.

[0028]  Simultaneously, the microcontroller actuates multiple telescopic links 104 (ranging from 4 to 6 in numbers) incorporated downwardly on the rod 103 to extend and position a rectangular plate 105 attached at ends of each link, in contact with the snow. The extension of the links 104 is powered by a pneumatic unit that includes an air compressor, air cylinder, air valves and piston which works in collaboration to aid in extension and retraction of the links 104.

[0029] The air compressor used herein extract the air from surrounding and increases the pressure of the air by reducing the volume of the air. The air compressor is consisting of two main parts including a motor and a pump. The motor powers the compressor pump which uses the energy from the motor drive to draw in atmospheric air and compress to elevated pressure. The compressed air is then sent through a discharge tube into the cylinder across the valve. The compressed air in the cylinder tends to pushes out the piston to extend. The piston is attached to the links 104, wherein the extension of the piston corresponds to the extension of the links 104 in order to establish physical contact of the plates 105 with the snow.

[0030]  Once the plates 105 are positioned in contact with the snow, the microcontroller actuates a hinge 106 configured between each of the plates 105 and the links 104 to tilt the plates 105 in order to remove the snow during the translation of the rod 103. The hinges 106 integrates an electric motor with a traditional hinge mechanism to enable controlled, automated rotational movement of the plates 105 around a fixed axis.

[0031]  The hinge joint comprises of a pair of leaf that are screwed with the surface of the plates 105 and the links 104. The leafs are connected with each other by means of a cylindrical member integrated with a shaft coupled with a DC (Direct Current) motor to provide required movement to the hinges 106. The rotation of the shaft in clockwise and anti-clockwise direction provides required tilting movement to the hinges 106, that in turn tilt the plates 105 for effectively removing the snow during the translation of the rod 103 along the surface of the solar panel.

[0032]  Synchronously, the microcontroller in association with a moisture sensor embedded in the frame 101, detects moisture on the solar panel. The moisture sensor used herein is a non-contact moisture sensor which operate based on capacitance principle. An electromagnetic field is generated by an oscillator circuit within the sensor. This field extends to the solar panel. When the solar panel is dry, its dielectric constant is relatively low. However, when moisture is present, the dielectric constant increases. This change in dielectric constant alters the capacitance between the sensor and the surface. The sensor measures the changes in capacitance caused by the presence of moisture. This change is converted into an electrical signal, which is then transferred to the linked microcontroller for interpretation.

[0033] The microcontroller processes the signals received from the moisture sensor in order to determine the moisture level of the solar panel and accordingly actuates multiple hot air blowers 108 (ranging from 2 to 4 in numbers) installed along the frame 101 for blowing air onto the solar panel for drying of the solar panel. The air blowers 108 used herein consists of a motor, fan blades, an air intake, and an outlet nozzle. When the microcontroller activates the blower, the motor drives the fan blades to rotate at high speed, drawing air through the intake. The blades push this air towards the outlet nozzle, creating a focused stream of air. This air is then directed towards the solar panel, in order to dry the solar panel.

[0034]  Further, the microcontroller by means of an LDR (light dependent resistor) provided with the frame 101, detects an ambient light level. The LDR (light dependent resistor) comprises of a photodiode, wherein the photodiode is capable of measuring intensity of light in proximity of the solar panel, when beam of light strikes the photodiode then the photodiode has a tendency to loosen electrons causing an electric current to flow. More the intensity of light, stronger is the electric current generated by the sensor which is further transmitted to the microcontroller.
 
[0035]  The microcontroller interprets the magnitude of the generated current to determine the intensity of the ambient light in proximity of the solar panel and compares the determined intensity level with a threshold level that is pre-feed in the database of the microcontroller. In case the determined intensity of light is below the threshold level, the microcontroller generates a command to activate multiple LEDs 110 (Light Emitting Diode) (ranging from 4 to 6 in numbers) mounted on the frame 101 to glow for providing optimal illumination.

[0036]  The LED (Light Emitting Diode) light is a two-lead semiconductor light source also known as p-n junction which produce the lighting when constant voltage is supplied across the diode. When the voltage is supplied across the diode, the electrons recombine with the electrons hole in the diode which result in conversion of electron into photons (which is another form of light) to glow and provide illumination.

The communication module used herein includes, but not limited to Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) module, Bluetooth module, GSM (Global System for Mobile Communication) module.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to an automated paver tile manufacturing device that is capable of providing a means to manufacture paver tiles as per user requirement in an automated manner.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002]  Paver tile manufacturing involves the production of durable, versatile tiles used primarily for outdoor applications such as walkways, patios, and driveways. The process typically begins with the selection of high-quality raw materials, including clay, concrete, or stone, which are then mixed, shaped, and cured to achieve the desired strength and aesthetic. Modern manufacturing techniques may incorporate advanced technologies like automated molding and pressing, along with the use of pigments and finishes to enhance appearance and weather resistance. As sustainability becomes increasingly important, manufacturers are also exploring eco-friendly materials and practices, such as recycled content and energy-efficient production methods. This industry not only caters to residential needs but also serves commercial projects, contributing significantly to the landscape of urban and suburban environments.

[0003]  Traditional paver tile manufacturing methods often involve hand-molding clay or concrete mixtures into shapes, followed by air drying and firing in kilns for clay tiles or curing for concrete. While these artisanal techniques allow for unique designs and high craftsmanship, they come with several issues. The reliance on manual labor can lead to inconsistencies in quality and dimensions, while the firing process for clay tiles consumes significant energy and can result in variable color outcomes. Additionally, the time-consuming nature of hand production limits scalability, making the process challenging to meet high demand. Furthermore, traditional methods may not adhere to modern sustainability standards, raising concerns about environmental impact and resource efficiency.

[0004] US10844551B2 discloses a method for manufacturing of paver block and bricks includes addition of cementitious materials, additives, and binding materials. The method also includes homogenization of the added materials to obtain a first mixture, addition of a hardener solution to the first mixture, mixing the first mixture with the hardener solution for 5 to 30 minutes to obtain a second mixture, casting the second mixture into a mold to obtain a solidified part, and curing the solidified part in atmospheric air. Though US’551 relates to a method for manufacturing of paver blocks and bricks from industrial waste, however, the cited art lacks in providing a means to level mixture for precise and accurate manufacturing of paver tiles.
 
[0005] Conventionally, many devices have been developed to facilitate in manufacturing of paver tile, however, the prior arts mentioned above have limitations pertaining to providing a means to level mixture for precise and accurate manufacturing of paver tiles.

[0006] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that requires to be capable of providing a means to generate vibrations for levelling mixture to produce and manufacture paver tiles in utmost accuracy and precision.

[0008]  An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing a means to manufacture paver tiles as per user requirement in an automated manner.

[0009] Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing a means to mix water, sand and mixture into a mixture and accordingly adjust to cut and shape the mixture into tiles. 

[0010]  Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing a means to generate vibrations for levelling mixture to produce and manufacture paver tiles in utmost accuracy and precision.

[0022]  The proposed device includes a housing 101 placed over a ground surface via multiple legs 102 that ranges from (2 to 4 in numbers). The housing 101 serves as the core structure and is made up of lightweight yet robust metals like aluminium or high-strength plastics. These materials provide structural integrity while keeping the device manageable in weight for ease of use and portability. The outer layer of the housing 101 is made from durable and washable materials which includes but not limited to fabric, leather, vinyl, or synthetic materials. The housing 101 is configured with a multi-sectioned chamber 103 accessed by a user for filling water, sand, cement required to manufacture paver tiles. 

[0023]  The housing 101 is installed with a mixing container 104 connected to the chamber 103 via a conduit 105, wherein each section of the chamber 103 is installed with an electronic valve 106 commanded by an inbuilt microcontroller for dispensing a regulated amount of the water, sand and cement into the conduit 105 that further gets transferred into the container 104. The electronic valve 106 comprises of a gate and a magnetic coil which uses electricity from the microcontroller to generate the force to control the opening /closing of the gate to dispense the regulated amount of the water, sand and cement into the conduit 105 that further gets transferred into the container 104.

[0024]  The housing 101 is installed with a touch interactive display panel 112 commanded by the microcontroller for enabling the user to provide input specs related to manufacturing of the paver tiles. When the user accesses the touch interactive display panel 112 for providing inputs related to manufacturing of the paver tiles, then an internal circuitry of the display panel 112 senses those touches of the user and synchronically, the internal circuitry automatically converts the touch responses into electric signals and then transmits those signals to the microcontroller. The microcontroller further analyses the signals and actuates the display panel 112 for enabling the user in providing inputs related to manufacturing of the paver tiles. Based on processing of the inputs provided by the user, the microcontroller regulates actuation of the valve 106 for dispensing the water, sand and the cement.

[0025]  The chamber 103 is installed with a motorized stirrer 107 commanded by the microcontroller for mixing water, sand and the cement to produce mortar mixture. The motorized stirrer 107 comprises of a motor and a pair of blades. The microcontroller powers the motor that further drives the pair of blades to rotate on axis to produce mortar mixture. Simultaneously, the microcontroller commands a suction pump 108 installed in the container 104 for withdrawing the mixture and dispensing the mixture into a tray 109 installed over the housing 101. 

[0026]  The suction pump 108 works on the principle of flow of air from area of high pressure to area of low pressure. An electric motor is attached to a fan that spins the fan at high velocities. The fast-spinning fan creates a region of low pressure inside the conduit 105 of the suction unit. Air, along with the mixture is sucked into the conduit 105 and thus withdrawing and dispense the mixture within the tray 109 connected with the pump 108 via a pipe. The tray 109 is installed with a vibration unit 113 commanded by the microcontroller for levelling the mixture in the tray 109. The vibration units 113 is a device for subjecting a system to the action of moving or causing to move back and forth or from side to side very quickly leading to controlled and reproducible vibrations for levelling the mixture in the tray 109.

[0027]  The tray 109 is configured with a concrete mold 110 via a motorized hinge joint commanded by the microcontroller for placing the mold 110 in the tray 109 for cutting and shaping the mixture into the tiles. The motorized hinge joints used herein, are piece of metal that joins two sides or items together and opens/closes the mold by revolving along the longitudinal axis whose operation is governed by a DC motor for placing the mold 110 in the tray 109 for cutting and shaping the mixture into the tiles.

[0028] The tray 109 is integrated with a moisture sensor for monitoring moisture level of the mixture. The moisture sensor uses capacitance to measure dielectric permittivity of the mixture. In mixture, dielectric permittivity is a function of the water content. The moisture sensor creates a voltage proportional to the dielectric permittivity, and therefore the water content of the plate is measured. The moisture sensor transmits the signals to the microcontroller. The microcontroller processes the received data in order to determine the presence of the moisture in the mixture. In case, the detected level receded a threshold level, the microcontroller commands a speaker 111 installed on the housing 101 for notifying the user to collect the shaped tiles.

[0029]  The speaker 111 comprises of a voice coil and a permanent magnet. The microcontroller actuates the speaker 111 thereby generating electrical current via the voice coil which further produces an electric field that interacts with the magnetic field of the permanent magnet attached to the speaker 111. Due to attraction and repelling of like charges with each other, an audio signal is sent via the voice coil due to which, a musical waveform is produced that moves up and down, the voice coil gets attracted and repelled by the permanent magnet. Due to attraction and repelling of the voice coil by the permanent magnet, a cone attached with the voice coil moves back and forth creating pressure waves in the air perceiving as voice commands from the speaker 111 to produce audio signals to notify the user to collect the shaped tiles.

[0030]  The base portion of the tray 109 is configured with multiple pneumatic pins 114 that ranges from (2 to 4 in numbers), commanded by the microcontroller to extend for detaching the tiles from the tray 109. The pneumatic pins 114 are powered by pneumatic unit that includes an air compressor, air cylinder, air valves 106 and piston which works in collaboration to aid in extension and retraction of the pins 114 for detaching the tiles from the tray 109. The housing 101 is configured with a robotic gripper 115 commanded by the microcontroller for withdrawing the manufactured tiles from the tray 109 and store the tiles in a box arranged in the housing 101. These arms are usually made of durable materials like metal or plastic to provide strength and flexibility. Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to an autonomous potholes repairing device that repair a pothole present over a road surface in an automated manner by detecting the presence of pothole and cleaning and filling the pothole with an appropriate amount of mortar mixture required as per the volume of the pothole in an automated manner.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002]  Potholes are depressions or holes in road surfaces caused by the wear and tear of traffic and the natural elements, such as water and temperature changes. When water seeps into cracks in the pavement and expands during freezing, it weakens the road material, eventually causing chunks to break away, forming potholes. These potholes create hazards for drivers and pedestrians, potentially causing vehicle damage, accidents, and injuries. They also disrupt traffic flow. It is crucial to repair potholes promptly to maintain road safety, prevent further infrastructure damage, and minimize costs associated with more extensive repairs in the future.

[0003] Traditionally, potholes are repaired using manual methods and basic tools. Workers clean the pothole by removing loose debris and dirt using shovels or brooms. Next, they apply a patching material, typically asphalt or concrete, into the hole. The material is then leveled and compacted with hand tampers or rollers to ensure a smooth surface. While effective, these methods are labor-intensive and time-consuming, requiring significant manual effort for cleaning, filling, and compacting. The repairs are often temporary, as the materials used do not bond well or withstand extreme weather conditions, leading to frequent reoccurrence of potholes. Additionally, manual repairs cause traffic disruptions, increasing the risk of accidents. Inconsistent application and compaction result in uneven surfaces, compromising the durability of the repair.

[0004] CN215925569U discloses about a pothole repairing device for rural road maintenance, which comprises a bottom plate, a protective barrel fixedly connected to the upper surface of the bottom plate, a heating barrel fixedly connected in the protective barrel, a heating pipe spirally wound on the outer wall of the heating barrel, a support frame arranged on one side of the protective barrel, and a heating device arranged on the upper surface of the support frame. The supporting plate is fixedly connected with a fixing plate, an air cylinder is arranged on the upper surface of the fixing plate, the extending end of the air cylinder penetrates through the fixing plate to be detachably connected with a material receiving barrel, a discharging port is formed in the lower end of the material receiving barrel, a plurality of universal wheels are fixedly connected to the lower surface of the bottom plate, and a push rod used for pushing the device is fixedly connected to the side wall of the bottom plate. The pothole repairing device is used for solving the problem that an existing pothole repairing device cannot conduct pothole repairing automatically. Although, CN’569 discloses about an invention that relates to a pothole repairing device for rural road maintenance. However, the cited invention lacks in repairing the potholes in an automated manner by automatically filling the pothole.

[0005] CN209568351U discloses about a pothole repairing device for road maintenance. Including a mobile station, a plurality of locking type universal wheels are arranged at the lower end of the moving table; the upper end of the moving table is fixedly connected with a vertical column; two push rods are fixedly connected to the side wall of the vertical column; a cross rod is arranged between the two push rods; and the left end and the right end of the cross rod are connected with two push rods correspondingly, a moving mechanism is arranged at the upper end of the moving table, a transverse moving mechanism is fixedly connected to the upper end of the moving mechanism, a pressing mechanism is fixedly connected to the side wall of the side wall of the transverse moving mechanism, and a stirring mechanism is fixedly connected to the upper end of the vertical column. Through the use of the moving mechanism, the transverse moving mechanism and the pressing mechanism, when materials are poured onto a road surface, the ceramic heating plate can flatten the materials through the first electric sliding rail and the second electric sliding rail, and the materials can be pressed through the third electric sliding rail, so that the small-sized damaged road surface can be maintained. Though, CN’351 discloses about an invention that relates to a pothole repairing device for road maintenance. However, the cited invention lacks in automatically removing the dust and debris from the pothole before repairing the pothole.
 
[0006] Conventionally, many devices have been developed that are capable of assisting a user in repairing/filling potholes. However, these devices are incapable of repairing the potholes in an automated manner by automatically filling the pothole with mortar mixture. Additionally, these existing devices also fail in leveling the repaired pothole in an automated manner.

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that requires to be capable of repairing/maintain potholes present over a road in an automated manner without the need of any manual interference by automatically detecting the pothole and filling the pothole with mortar mixture. In addition, the developed device also needs to prepare a specific amount mortar mixture required for filling the pothole as per the volume of the pothole.

 OBJECTS OF THE INVENTION

[0008]  The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]  An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of repairing/maintaining a pothole present over the surface of a road by automatically detecting the potholes and filling mortar mixture into the pothole in an automated manner, thereby reducing manual efforts and consumption of time in the overall process.

[0010] Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of detecting the deposition of dust/dirt into the pothole and accordingly provide a means for extracting the dust/dirt from the pothole.

[0011]  Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of detecting irregularities and dimensions of the pothole and accordingly evaluates an amount of mortar mixture required for filling the pothole, thereby ensures optimal usage of resources and minimizing waste.
