Description:DETAILED DESCRIPTION   
[0015] This disclosure provides a composition and method for addressing neurobehavioral alterations caused by prolonged exposure to chronic unpredictable stress. The core component of the composition is Piceatannol, a naturally occurring polyphenol known for its antioxidant, anti-aging, and anti-inflammatory properties. Piceatannol has also shown promise in regulating neurotransmitter imbalances, rescuing mitochondrial biogenesis, and inhibiting oxidative stress-induced autophagy, which are key factors in neurobehavioral disorders. Its ability to target underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms makes it a potential therapeutic agent for managing conditions like anxiety, depression, and memory dysfunction. Unlike conventional treatments, Piceatannol focuses on disease-modifying effects, addressing the root causes rather than merely alleviating symptoms. This makes it a promising compound for treating chronic unpredictable stress and related neurobehavioral alterations. An oral formulation of Piceatannol is prepared to ensure ease of administration, patient compliance, and efficient systemic absorption. Oral dosage forms like tablets and capsules are non-invasive, convenient, and widely accepted by patients, making them suitable for long-term use in managing chronic conditions. This route provides controlled and consistent delivery of the active ingredient, enhancing its bioavailability and therapeutic effectiveness. Additionally, oral formulations can be tailored to include pharmaceutically acceptable excipients that stabilize Piceatannol, improve its solubility, and ensure its stability during storage and administration. By using an oral formulation, the therapeutic potential of Piceatannol can be maximized, providing a practical and effective approach to addressing neurobehavioral alterations caused by chronic stress. 
[0016] The formulation process may enhance the therapeutic potential of Piceatannol, providing neuroprotective effects and targeting various neurological and behavioral aspects. The formulation can rescue mitochondrial biogenesis, inhibit oxidative stress-induced autophagy, mitigate neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration, and improve anxiety, depression, and memory dysfunction. The composition includes pharmaceutically acceptable excipients to enhance its stability, consistency, and therapeutic effectiveness. 
[0017] In an embodiment, the composition can include Microcrystalline Cellulose as a filler or bulking agent in the amount of 30–60% w/w; a diluent such as Lactose Monohydrate, Sorbitol, Mannitol, or Sucrose in the amount of 20–30% w/w; a disintegrant such as Croscarmellose Sodium, Sodium Starch Glycolate, Crospovidone, or Alginic Acid in the amount of 2–5% w/w; a binder such as Povidone (K30), Hydroxypropyl Cellulose, Starch Paste, or Gelatin in the amount of 2–5% w/w; a lubricant such as Magnesium Stearate, Stearic Acid, Sodium Stearyl Fumarate, or Talc in the amount of 0.5–2% w/w; and a glidant such as Colloidal Silicon Dioxide, Talc, Magnesium Silicate, or Calcium Silicate in the amount of 0.2–1% w/w. These excipients ensure the formulation's effectiveness, stability, and ease of administration.
[0018] In a preferred embodiment, the composition can comprise microcrystalline cellulose as a filler/bulking agent, present in an amount of 30–60% w/w; lactose monohydrate as a diluent, present in an amount of 20–30% w/w; croscarmellose sodium as a disintegrant, present in an amount of 2–5% w/w; povidone (k30) as a binder, present in an amount of 2–5% w/w; magnesium stearate as a lubricant, present in an amount of 0.5–2% w/w; and colloidal silicon dioxide as a glidant, present in an amount of 0.2–1% w/w. Abstract:

A novel composition for treating osteoporosis is disclosed, comprising Tributyrin and Calcitriol in specific concentration ranges, along with a sterile phosphate-buffered saline solvent, polysorbate 80, glycerin, benzyl alcohol, and pH-adjusting agents. This composition targets HDAC-6 and VDR pathways to enhance bone remodeling, decrease osteoclast activity, and mitigate osteoporosis symptoms. It is formulated for administration during the last 14 days of a 28-day protocol and is effective in increasing bone mineral density and improving serum biomarkers associated with bone health. The composition demonstrates superior efficacy compared to monotherapy approaches. Reference Fig 1

[0050] In an extension of this work, an injectable formulation for treating osteoporosis has been developed, incorporating Tributyrin and Calcitriol in specific concentrations optimized for efficacy. The formulation includes sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) as the primary solvent, ensuring isotonicity and stability of the active components. Polysorbate 80 is employed as a solubilizer, facilitating the homogenous distribution of Tributyrin within the solution, with a concentration range of 0.1–0.5% w/v. Glycerin is added in a concentration range of 0.5–2% w/v to enhance stability and isotonicity, contributing to the overall safety and consistency of the formulation. Benzyl alcohol, in a concentration range of 0.5–1% w/v, acts as a preservative to prevent microbial contamination, ensuring the sterility and longevity of the injectable solution. To maintain the chemical stability of the active ingredients and ensure compatibility, the pH of the formulation is adjusted to a range of 6.8–7.2 using sodium hydroxide or hydrochloric acid. Additionally, the tonicity of the formulation is carefully controlled to match the osmolarity of human plasma, approximately 290 mOsm/L, to avoid tissue irritation or osmotic stress. Tonicity is verified using freezing point depression osmometry or calculated based on the contributions of PBS and glycerin, ensuring the injectable formulation is isotonic and safe for administration. This carefully crafted composition targets the HDAC-6 and VDR pathways, providing a synergistic therapeutic approach that enhances bone remodeling, decreases osteoclast activity, and mitigates osteoporosis symptoms more effectively than traditional monotherapies. The formulation demonstrates superior efficacy, as evidenced by improvements in bone mineral density and serum biomarkers, supporting its potential as a novel and effective treatment for osteoporosis.

[0053] Example 2: The process for preparing the injectable formulation for treating osteoporosis involves a series of carefully controlled steps to ensure stability, homogeneity, and safety. Initially, sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) is prepared as the primary solvent, providing a stable isotonic medium for the active ingredients. Tributyrin and Calcitriol are then added to the PBS in their respective concentration ranges, with Tributyrin at 25–50 mg/mL and Calcitriol at 10–30 IU/mL. To facilitate the uniform solubilization of Tributyrin within the aqueous medium, polysorbate 80 is incorporated in a concentration range of 0.1–0.5% w/v, ensuring homogeneity of the formulation. Glycerin, added in a concentration range of 0.5–2% w/v, not only enhances the stability of the formulation but also contributes to its isotonicity. Benzyl alcohol, at a concentration range of 0.5–1% w/v, is included as a preservative to prevent microbial contamination and extend the shelf life of the product.

[0054] Once all the components are mixed, the pH of the formulation is adjusted to a range of 6.8–7.2 using sodium hydroxide or hydrochloric acid to maintain the chemical stability of the active ingredients. The mixture is then subjected to sterile filtration through a 0.22 µm filter to remove particulate matter and ensure sterility. To confirm the isotonicity of the solution, the osmolarity is measured using freezing point depression osmometry or calculated based on the contributions of PBS and glycerin, ensuring the final formulation matches the osmolarity of human plasma (~290 mOsm/L). The sterile solution is then filled into amber glass vials to protect the light-sensitive Calcitriol, sealed with rubber stoppers and aluminum caps under aseptic conditions. The prepared vials undergo terminal sterilization to ensure microbiological safety, completing the process for the formulation. This meticulous preparation ensures a stable, safe, and effective injectable product designed to enhance bone remodeling and mitigate osteoporosis symptoms.

Some embodiments of this disclosure, illustrating all its features, will now be discussed in detail. The words "comprising," "having," "containing," and "including," and other forms thereof, are intended to be equivalent in meaning and be open ended in that an item or items following any one of these words is not meant to be an exhaustive listing of such item or items, or meant to be limited to only the listed item or items.
For purposes of the present invention, the terms "active agent", "drug" , “active” “bioactive” “medicament” “active pharmaceutical ingredient”  are used interchangeably, and are meant to encompass a single essential oil contained in the topical spray formulations of the invention.
The term "topical" and its derivatives as used herein refer to directly laying on or spreading on the skin in need of the treatment, e.g., by use of the hands or an applicator.
The term "efficacy" as used herein refers to the extent to which a treatment produces a beneficial result, e.g., an improvement in one or more symptoms of the disease. In one embodiment, efficacy is evaluated by lesion counting, which is a current practice to assess severity of acne.
A "therapeutically effective amount" means the amount that, when administered to an animal for treating a disease, is sufficient to effect treatment for that disease.
The term “nanoformulation” refers to a preparation in which the active components, such as drugs or bioactive compounds, are encapsulated, loaded, or embedded in nanoscale carriers or systems. These carriers typically range in size from 1 to 1000 nanometers (nm) 
The term “polymer matrix” refers to a continuous three-dimensional network or structure composed of polymeric materials that act as a carrier or scaffold for encapsulating and stabilizing active ingredients. Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION
This invention relates to blockchain technology, specifically to systems and methods for tracking cryptocurrency transactions. The invention focuses on enhancing transparency, risk assessment, and detecting obfuscation techniques such as mixers and tumblers.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
The rapid adoption of blockchain technology has transformed financial transactions by providing decentralized and secure platforms for digital assets. However, the inherent anonymity in cryptocurrency transactions has led to challenges in tracking and assessing risks associated with illicit activities. Current solutions lack dynamic and intuitive visualization tools to represent transaction flows effectively, leaving users unable to interpret complex transaction data.
Obfuscation techniques, such as mixers and tumblers, further exacerbate these issues by concealing the origins and destinations of funds. Existing systems also struggle with accurately assessing risks associated with wallet behaviors, particularly those employing diverse transaction patterns. Without robust tools to identify these activities, users and regulators face significant hurdles in monitoring blockchain networks.
To address these limitations, this invention introduces a system that provides dynamic flowchart visualizations, advanced risk scoring, and obfuscation detection algorithms. The system integrates front-end visualization, backend data processing, and a database for transaction histories, empowering users to gain actionable insights into cryptocurrency transactions.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
This invention provides a system for tracking and visualizing cryptocurrency transactions, incorporating dynamic flowchart generation, risk scoring, and detection of obfuscation techniques. The system comprises a frontend user interface built with React.js, a Node.js backend for processing and API integration, and a NoSQL database for storing transaction histories. The dynamic flowchart feature represents transactions as nodes and directed edges, allowing users to interact with the data through hover and click actions.
The risk scoring mechanism evaluates wallet behaviors using factors such as transaction frequency, size, and obfuscation detection. It assigns a risk score on a scale of 1 to 10, categorizing wallets into low, moderate, or high-risk profiles. The obfuscation detection algorithm identifies suspicious transactions by analyzing patterns and comparing them with known mixer activities. The system is designed with responsive user interfaces and supports seamless navigation, offering a robust solution for blockchain transparency and security.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The invention introduces a comprehensive system for tracking cryptocurrency transactions, designed to enhance transparency and security. The system comprises three primary components: a React.js-based frontend, a Node.js backend, and a NoSQL database. The frontend offers an intuitive interface where users can visualize transaction flows through dynamic flowcharts. Each transaction is represented as a node, with edges depicting fund transfers. Users can interact with the flowcharts by hovering for tooltips or clicking to explore related nodes and histories.
The backend processes data retrieved from blockchain APIs such as Etherscan. It employs asynchronous calls to fetch transaction histories, wallet balances, and risk-related data. This data is processed to generate flowcharts and risk scores, which are rendered on the user interface. The NoSQL database ensures efficient storage and retrieval of transaction records, supporting scalability and performance.
The risk scoring mechanism evaluates wallets based on transaction patterns, recipient diversity, and obfuscation activities. Scores are assigned on a scale of 1 to 10, categorizing wallets into low, moderate, or high-risk profiles. The obfuscation detection algorithm analyzes transaction paths for patterns indicative of mixers and tumblers. Criteria include multiple inputs and outputs or rapid, timed transactions. Detected transactions are flagged for further analysis, providing users with actionable insights into potential risks.
Experimental results demonstrate the system’s effectiveness, with an average data retrieval time of 2 seconds and a user satisfaction rate of 85%. The responsive design ensures usability across devices, enabling users to navigate transaction data seamlessly. Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION
This invention relates to data extraction technologies, specifically focusing on a tool designed to retrieve user data from multiple social media platforms. By integrating web scraping techniques and automated workflows, the invention supports seamless data retrieval for analysis and reporting across platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Twitter, and Telegram.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
The growing reliance on social media platforms for personal and professional interactions has created a demand for tools that can efficiently aggregate and analyze user data. Current solutions often target individual platforms, making the data extraction process inefficient and fragmented. These tools typically lack support for multiple platforms, unified workflows, and robust error-handling mechanisms, limiting their usability and scope.
With social media platforms enforcing unique authentication protocols and data access restrictions, the need for a universal solution becomes critical. By automating login procedures, handling platform-specific checkpoints, and managing data storage systematically, this invention provides a streamlined approach to cross-platform data extraction. The tool addresses critical gaps in existing methods, enabling users to extract and analyze their social media data with greater accuracy and efficiency.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
This invention introduces a Universal Social Media Extractor, a tool designed to extract user data from multiple social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Twitter, and Telegram. The system employs web scraping techniques, automated workflows, and error-handling mechanisms to ensure seamless data retrieval. It captures user information, including friend lists, messages, posts, group memberships, and engagement metrics, storing it in a centralized database for further analysis.
The system architecture comprises platform-specific modules tailored to address unique authentication protocols and data retrieval methods. Features such as automated scrolling, screenshot capture, and checkpoint handling ensure comprehensive data extraction. Experimental results demonstrate high accuracy rates across platforms, with friend list retrieval achieving 98% accuracy on Facebook and message extraction on Instagram reaching 85%.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
The Universal Social Media Extractor is a comprehensive tool for extracting user data from multiple social media platforms. The system's architecture is modular, with platform-specific components that handle unique authentication protocols and data retrieval methods. The core functionalities are detailed below:
The tool begins by allowing users to select the desired platform, such as Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Twitter, or Telegram. Each platform module employs web scraping techniques powered by Python and Selenium. Automated login processes ensure seamless access, handling checkpoints through prompts or automatic retries. The system navigates through the platform, extracting user data such as friend lists, messages, posts, and group memberships. Screenshots are captured during the extraction process to enhance reporting.
The extracted data is stored in a centralized database, enabling organized analysis and reporting. Advanced error-handling mechanisms, including logging and retry protocols, ensure minimal data loss during the process. For example, if a checkpoint is encountered, the system pauses and prompts the user to resolve it before resuming data retrieval. This mechanism ensures continuity and accuracy in data extraction.
Experimental results validate the tool’s efficiency. On Facebook, the friend list extraction achieved a 98% accuracy rate, while Instagram message retrieval succeeded with 85% accuracy. Error handling proved effective, logging all issues and enabling successful retries. The tool demonstrated scalability across different operating systems, including Windows and Linux, ensuring broad applicability.
The Universal Social Media Extractor also incorporates a reporting feature, organizing captured screenshots and extracted data into structured reports. These reports provide actionable insights, helping users analyze their social media presence effectively. The tool’s architecture and workflows establish it as a reliable and versatile solution for multi-platform data extraction.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION
This invention relates to artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies, specifically to the integration of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and natural language processing (NLP) for developing an advanced chatbot capable of recognizing images and generating meaningful textual responses.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
The growing demand for intelligent systems that bridge the gap between visual and textual communication has led to advancements in AI-powered chatbots. Existing systems, while effective in text-based interactions, struggle with understanding and interpreting visual information. The limitations in current chatbots include lack of integration between image recognition and dialogue generation, limited knowledge bases, and inadequate contextual understanding.
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have significantly improved image analysis capabilities, while transformers and other NLP advancements enable more nuanced textual interactions. However, the integration of these technologies to create a seamless, interactive chatbot remains a challenge. NeoChat addresses these limitations by combining CNNs for image recognition and NLP for dialogue generation, delivering a unified platform for visual communication and enhanced accessibility.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
NeoChat introduces a sophisticated chatbot that integrates convolutional neural networks for image analysis and natural language processing for dialogue generation. The invention enables users to input images, which are analyzed by the CNN model to extract features and generate textual descriptions. These descriptions are then processed by the NLP model to create informative and contextually accurate responses.
The chatbot leverages advanced AI architectures, including TensorFlow, to support robust training and optimization. The system incorporates features like voice activation, speech-to-text processing, and real-time webcam integration, providing an intuitive and interactive user experience. NeoChat's potential applications range from visual search and captioning to interactive storytelling and educational tools.
ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION
NeoChat offers several advantages that establish it as a pioneering solution in visual communication and information sharing. By integrating image recognition and dialogue generation, the chatbot facilitates seamless interaction between users and visual content. Its advanced CNN model ensures high accuracy in feature extraction, enabling detailed and contextually rich image descriptions.
The NLP model enhances the chatbot’s ability to interpret and respond to user queries with precision, providing insightful and relevant information. Features like voice activation and real-time image input via webcam enhance accessibility and user engagement, making NeoChat suitable for a diverse audience. The system’s scalability and adaptability for various applications, such as education, healthcare, and e-commerce, further highlight its transformative potential.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION
NeoChat is a comprehensive system designed to integrate convolutional neural networks and natural language processing for advanced image recognition and dialogue generation. The system’s architecture is built on TensorFlow, providing a robust framework for training and optimizing the AI models.
The convolutional image recognizer forms the core of NeoChat’s computer vision module. It employs convolutional layers to extract features such as edges, textures, and patterns, followed by pooling layers to reduce dimensionality and improve efficiency. Fully connected layers synthesize these features into textual descriptions that encapsulate the image’s content.
The natural language processing module interprets the generated text, utilizing word embedding to transform words into numerical vectors. RNNs process sequential information to maintain context, while transformers enable the model to understand long-range dependencies, ensuring coherent and contextually relevant responses.
NeoChat’s technical architecture integrates image recognition and NLP workflows seamlessly. The user provides an image input, which the CNN model processes to generate a textual description. This description is analyzed by the NLP module, which formulates a response tailored to the user’s query. The chatbot also incorporates voice activation and real-time webcam integration, enhancing accessibility and interactivity.
Simulation and evaluation tests demonstrate NeoChat’s effectiveness, achieving 95% accuracy in image recognition and 82% in question answering. These metrics underscore the system’s reliability and applicability across various domains.

Abstract:
Abstract:

A paper-based microfluidic device (µPAD) has been developed for the quantification of vitamin B1. The device utilizes a paper substrate with hydrophobic and hydrophilic zones, optimized to create channels for reagent interaction. The hydrophobic zones are formed using molten beeswax. A colorimetric assay involving thiamine B1 and phenol red is employed, producing a yellow color with intensity proportional to vitamin B1 concentration. The assay demonstrates high repeatability and sensitivity, with a limit of detection of 8.065 ppm and a limit of quantification of 24.438 ppm. The µPAD is portable, economical, and easy to use, requiring minimal solvents and no specialized training. It is categorized as a Lab-on-Chip instrument suitable for point-of-care chemical analysis. Description:DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION 
Some embodiments of this disclosure, illustrating all its features, will now be discussed in detail. The words "comprising," "having," "containing," and "including," and other forms thereof, are intended to be equivalent in meaning and be open ended in that an item or items following any one of these words is not meant to be an exhaustive listing of such item or items, or meant to be limited to only the listed item or items.
For purposes of the present invention, the terms "active agent", "drug" , “active” “bioactive” “medicament” are used interchangeably, and are meant to encompass a single essential oil contained in the topical spray formulations of the invention.
The term “essential oil” refers to a concentrated hydrophobic liquid containing volatile (easily evaporated at normal temperatures) chemical compounds from plants. 
The term “Foeniculum vulgare” or “fennel” is used interchangeably hereinafter and refers to an herb with yellow flowers. In the present invention oil of fennel is used as an active ingredient for its anti-spasmodic and estrogenic activity. 
The term "topical" and its derivatives as used herein refer to directly laying on or spreading on the skin in need of the treatment, e.g., by use of the hands or an applicator.
The term "efficacy" as used herein refers to the extent to which a treatment produces a beneficial result, e.g., an improvement in one or more symptoms of the disease. In one embodiment, efficacy is evaluated by lesion counting, which is a current practice to assess severity of acne.
A "therapeutically effective amount" means the amount that, when administered to an animal for treating a disease, is sufficient to effect treatment for that disease.
The term "stable" refers to a minimal change in physical and chemical properties of the composition over time relative to when it is manufactured. Stability over time may be evaluated based on pre-defined criteria including assay of active and related compounds, appearance, color, and pH.
The term “film forming spray” refers to as a non-solid dosage form that produces a film in situ, i.e. after application on the skin or any other body surface. It contains the essential oil and film forming excipients in a vehicle which, upon contact with the skin, leaves behind a film of excipients along with the drug upon solvent evaporation. The formed film can either be a solid polymeric material that acts as matrix for sustained release of drug to the skin or a residual liquid film which is rapidly absorbed in the stratum corneum. 
Although any methods similar or equivalent to those described herein can be used in the practice or testing of embodiments of the present disclosure, the exemplary methods are now described. The described embodiments are merely exemplary of the disclosure, which may be embodied in various forms.
Various modifications to the embodiment will be readily apparent to those skilled in the art and the generic principles herein may be applied to other embodiments. However, one of ordinary skill in the art will readily recognize that the present disclosure is not intended to be limited to the embodiments illustrated, but is to be accorded the widest scope consistent with the principles and features described herein. 
An embodiment of the invention relates to an herbal antifungal spray film comprising:
a. An essential oil blend selected from but not limited to bergamot oil, clary sage oil, clove oil, eucalyptus oil, geranium oil, lavender oil, lemongrass oil, oregano oil, peppermint oil, tea tree oil, and thyme oil;
b. A polymer selected from but not limited to Methyl methacrylate polymer, Kollicoat 30D, Hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose (HPMC), Ethyl Cellulose, Hydroxy Propyl Cellulose, Poly Vinyl Pyrrolidone (PVP), Poly Vinyl Alcohol (PVA), Chitosan, Silicones, Polydimethylsiloxane or a combination thereof. 
c. A plasticizer selected from polyethylene glycol, glycerine, glycol, sorbitol, dibutyl phthalate, propylene glycol, triethyl citrate, polysorbate or a combination thereof and 
d. A solvent selected from organic solvents but not limited to iso-propyl alcohol, ethanol, acetone, fatty alcohols, iso-propyl myristate, ethyl acetate, benzyl alcohol, butanol or a combination thereof

Essential Oil Blend 
In an aspect of the embodiment, Essential oils (EO) reported to possess antifungal action efficacy against fungus related physiological outcomes like dryness, cell death, etc. were considered for the study. EO have been reported to possess bioactive constituents like terpenes, phenols, and aldehydes that contribute to their antifungal properties and these essential oils also help alleviate other physiological symptoms associated with fungal infections such as skin irritation, itching, burning sensation and blister effects. Considering this, EO were selected based on their antifungal properties (minimum inhibitory concentration; MIC) that could target fungal strain. The essential oils used in bergamot oil, clary sage oil, clove oil, eucalyptus oil, geranium oil, lavender oil, lemongrass oil, oregano oil, peppermint oil, tea tree oil, and thyme oil  were provided as a gift sample from Herbovive Private Limited.
In an aspect of embodiment, the essential oil blend composed of essential oils selected from bergamot oil, clary sage oil, clove oil, eucalyptus oil, geranium oil, lavender oil, lemongrass oil, oregano oil, peppermint oil, tea tree oil, and thyme oil. 
In a preferred aspect, the essential oil blend consisted of a combination of tea tree oil, geranium oil, peppermint, clove oil and lavender oil. 
The essential oil blend selected comprises of Tea Tree oil comprising of Terpinen-4-ol, 1,8-cineole as an active bio-constituent with antifungal and anti-irritation properties; Geranium oil consisting of Citronellol and geraniol as active bio-constituents with antifungal effects. Peppermint oil consisting of menthol and menthone with anti-itching and soothing effects. Clove oil consisting of Eugenol as an antifungal and cell regenerator. Lavender oil consisting of Linalool and linalyl acetate with antifungal properties and relief from burning and blistering. 
In an aspect, the essential oils are present in an amount of 3-45% v/v. In an aspect, tea tree oil is present in an amount of 1-20% v.v, geranium oil is present in an amount of 2-40% v/v, peppermint oil is present in an amount of 0.1-0.5% v/v, clove oil is present in an amount of 0.01-0.1% v/v and lavender oil is present in an amount of 0.1-0.5% v/v. 
In a preferred aspect of the embodiment, tea tree oil is present in an amount of 1% v/v, geranium oil in an amount of 8% v/v, peppermint oil in an amount of 0.2% v/v, peppermint oil in an amount of 0.2% v/v, clove oil in an amount of 0.05% v/v and lavender oil in an amount of 0.15% v/v. 
Polymers
In an aspect of the embodiment, the film forming spray includes an effective amount of a polymer to provide the desired release of active agent as described herein. The polymer may comprise hydrophilic polymers such as polyvinyl pyrollidone (also known as PVP, povidone or copovidone) or a derivative thereof, polyvinyl alcohol, polyvinyl acetate, water soluble gums, water soluble celluloses (e.g., hydroxypropylmethylcellulose, hydroxypropylcellulose, hydroxyethylcellulose and the like. 
In certain aspects, the film forming polymer may be comprised of a hydrophobic polymer  The polymer may comprise Methyl methacrylate polymer (Eudragit RL-100), polymeric methacrylates (Kollicoat 30D) hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose, ethyl cellulose, hydroxy propyl cellulose, poly vinyl pyrrolidone (PVP), poly vinyl alcohol (PVA), chitosan, silicones, polydimethylsiloxane and combinations of any of the foregoing. 
In preferred embodiments, the film forming polymer comprises a combination of ethyl cellulose and methyl methacrylate polymer (Eudragit RL-100). 
In a preferred aspect, ethyl Cellulose is used in concentrations ranging from 1% to 3% w/v, ethyl cellulose and serves as the primary film-forming agent. It imparts structural integrity to the film and ensures uniform coating during application.
In a preferred aspect, methyl methacrylate polymer Eudragit RS-100 is incorporated in concentrations of 1% to 5% w/v, this polymer enhances film flexibility and enables controlled release of the active ingredients. Its permeability properties help maintain the skin's natural moisture while delivering the antifungal agents effectively.
In preferred embodiments, the film forming polymer comprises a combination of methyl methacrylate polymer (Eudragit RS-100), and ethyl cellulose. 
Plasticizer 
In an aspect, the herbal antifungal spray film further comprises of one or more plasticizers. Suitable plasticizers include but are not limited to polyethylene glycol, glycerine, glycol, sorbitol, dibutyl phthalate, propylene glycol, triethyl citrate, polysorbate, and combinations of any of the foregoing. In an aspect, the plasticizer is added in concentrations ranging from 0.2% to 0.5% v/v, preferably - propylene glycol which enhances the elasticity of the film, preventing brittleness. Its plasticizing effect allows the film to adhere to the skin comfortably without cracking or flaking. Additionally, it contributes to the overall stability of the formulation by reducing the evaporation rate of the solvent during application.
Solvent 
The preferred solvent for the herbal antifungal spray film include either alone or combination of iso-propyl alcohol, ethanol, acetone, fatty alcohols, iso-propyl myristate, ethyl acetate, benzyl alcohol, butanol. The solvent concentration in the topical spray formulation can vary between about 20% to about 99% of the formulation. Preferably, the solvent system comprises of 50% to 70% v/v of ethanol which acts as a volatile solvent, ensuring rapid drying upon application. It also aids in dissolving both the polymers and essential oils, creating a homogenous formulation. The use of ethanol minimizes residue and supports quick film formation. 
Process
An embodiment of the invention relates to a process for preparing an herbal antifungal spray film, comprising the steps of: 
a. Adding the essential oil blend to the solvent to form a mixture I; 
b. Adding the film forming polymers to the solvent to form a mixture II; 
c. Mixing the mixture I to mixture II with stirring to form a mixture III; 
d. Adding a plasticizer and remaining solvent to mixture III to form a spray film. 

By integrating essential oils with proven antifungal properties into a polymer-based spray film, this invention aims to provide a safer, more effective, and user-compliant alternative for the management of fungal infections. The present invention aims to demonstrate the successful formulation of an essential oil-based spray film (F4) with promising potential for the management of Cutenous candidiasis. The optimized formulation exhibited desirable formulation characteristics, indicating its practical applicability. Additionally, it displayed significant antifungal activity against Candida albicans, surpassing that of the marketed preparation, suggesting its efficacy as a therapeutic alternative. The use of essential oils as the active ingredient in the spray film presents a natural and safer approach, potentially minimizing adverse effects associated with conventional antifungal therapies.

The solution was stirred continuously until it becomes clear, homogeneous and free from lumps or visible particles. [0030] The herbal toothpaste formulation described herein combines natural ingredients with antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and teeth whitening properties to provide an effective and biocompatible alternative to synthetic toothpaste. The primary active ingredients in the formulation are Zanthoxylum armatum stem, Psidii guajavae folium leaves, and Mangifea Indica leaves. These herbal components are carefully selected and combined in specific proportions to maximize their efficacy in addressing dental issues such as cavities, gum bleeding, oral infections, and tooth discoloration. The Zanthoxylum armatum stem constitutes 5–15% of the formulation, while Mangifea Indica leaves and Psidii guajavae folium leaves are used in the range of 10–30% each. The process begins with the preparation of the herbal active ingredients, which are cleaned, dried, and ground into fine powders. These powders are then mixed to create a herbal base, typically in the proportions of 10% Zanthoxylum armatum, 20% Mangifea Indica, and 20% Psidii guajavae folium. This base is combined with a natural binding agent, such as Tragacanth, which is used in the range of 0.5% to 2% of the total formulation, along with 50% of the total water. The mixture is stirred continuously until a smooth, homogeneous gel is formed. To further enhance the gel's properties, glycerine is gradually added and fully incorporated.

[0031] A separate solution of Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS) is prepared by dissolving it in 20% of the total water and stirring until completely dissolved. SLS, used in the range of 0.5% to 2% of the total formulation, serves as a foaming agent to enhance the user experience by aiding in the even distribution of the toothpaste during brushing. The SLS solution is then gently added to the gel to avoid premature foaming, ensuring even distribution throughout the mixture. The remaining water is added to the gel to achieve uniformity, and the mixture is blended using a homogenizer for 5–10 minutes, which ensures a smooth and stable texture suitable for application. After homogenization, the toothpaste mixture undergoes quality control, where its consistency, viscosity, and pH levels are verified. Adjustments are made as necessary to ensure that the product meets the required standards. The pH is typically adjusted to a value of approximately 6.2, ensuring safety for oral use and maintaining stability. The final formulation is evaluated for physical appearance, with the desired outcome being a smooth, greenish-brown paste with no sharp or abrasive particles. The foaming power of the toothpaste is measured at 58, while its moisture content is recorded at 38%. Spreadability tests reveal a spread of 3.8 cm in three minutes, indicating excellent usability. Once the mixture meets all quality standards, it is transferred into sealed containers to preserve its integrity and prevent contamination. The final product is stable, effective, and ready for distribution and consumer use. This natural toothpaste formulation not only addresses common dental issues but also avoids the adverse effects often associated with synthetic alternatives, offering a safe, effective, and environmentally friendly solution for oral care.

Example 3: Induction of the T2DM-induced Dementia 
Following a period of adaptive feeding for 2 days, the diabetic rat model was formed initially. Rats in the disease control group, all test treatment groups, and the standard control group were fed a high-fat diet for 4 weeks. On the last day of the 4th week, rats in each group began fasting, excluding water, at 5:00 PM, 1 day before the injection of STZ. At 9:00 am the next day, rats were injected with STZ (35 mg/kg b.w.) dissolved in freshly prepared 0.1 mol/L sodium citrate buffer (pH 4.4). After 72 h, fasting blood glucose (FBG) was measured by a portable glucometer from the tail vein. Rats with FBG levels of 11.1 mmol/L or higher were considered as a successfully induced diabetic model and were used in subsequent experiments.
Subsequently, the Alzheimer diabetic rat model was established. Seven days later, all diabetic rats were anesthetized with Ketamine (75mg/kg) in combination with Xylazine (25mg/kg) and fixed on a brain stereotaxic instrument. Two holes were drilled by a dental auger after defined points stereotaxically, specifically two points in bilateral hippocampal areas (behind the bregma 4.4 mm, meta 2.2 mm, deep 3.0 mm). The left hippocampus was localized first, followed by the right hippocampus. Rats were injected with Aß25–35 at 7.5 µL on each side. The escape latency in the Morris water maze and passive avoidance test were then evaluated to indicate the successful establishment of the Alzheimer diabetic rat model compared with the vehicle control group.
Disease control rats were treated with 4µ8c composition (5 & 10 mg/kg) and combination of Glimepiride (10 mg/kg) + Donepezil (1 mg/kg) for 30 days, respectively. During the same period, disease control group rats were fed a high-fat diet without drug treatment, and vehicle control rats were fed basic feed without any intervention, for a total of 30 days.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to a voltammetric non-enzymatic electrochemical sensing device featuring highly stable allylamine-capped CuNPs-fCNT composite coated on Au-sputtered strip electrodes is designed for rapid nitrate ion detection in soil and water. The device enables fast, reliable analysis (<5 minutes) from minimally processed, non-centrifuged samples, making it highly convenient for onsite periodic monitoring of soil and water. Its miniaturized design integrates seamlessly with smartphones via a pocket Potentiostat, ensuring ease of use by unskilled individuals. Farmers can utilize this device to accurately quantify nitrate levels, helping them regulate fertilizer use and prevent contamination of nearby water bodies, promoting sustainable agricultural practices and environmental protection.


BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
Excessive usage of nitrogen-containing fertilizers on agricultural fields leads to the percolation of soluble nitrate ions through soil which ultimately leaches into ground and surface water bodies, hence contaminating the water. The major conventional techniques for nitrate ion detection include ultraviolet-visible (UV-VIS) spectroscopy1, ion chromatography (IC) 2, enzymatic assay1, flow injection analysis3, and chemiluminescence4. However, these techniques are unsuitable for in situ and real-time onsite application, as they require several preprocessing techniques, bio receptors that face stability issues, bulky instrumentation suitable for laboratory purposes only, time-consuming steps, and the requirement of trained personnel. On the other hand, electrochemical sensors can achieve rapid and onsite detection of nitrate ions. Several non-enzymatic based nitrate ion sensing methods are reported, mainly featuring the usage of complex electrode surface modification steps. Along with that metal nanoparticles like copper (Cu) are the most efficient catalytic material for nitrate ion sensing. As a result, several Cu-based electrodes have been used for the detection of nitrate ion, including, Cu-coated bismuth bulk electrode, Cu-plated boron diamond electrode5, Cu-plated Cu wire6, Cu co-modified carbon fiber electrode7, Cu-rGO composite modified ITO electrode8 and Cu-PANI matrix modified GCE9. But Cu-based sensors suffer from storage stability issues due to the rapid oxidative nature of Cu nanoparticles and also most of the electrodes used in these works need laboratory setup not suitable for onsite field analysis settings. Additionally, numerous transition metals, including palladium (Pd), platinum (Pt), and silver (Ag), their alloys and composites, have been effectively used for nitrate ion detection8. However, their low abundance in nature and their high cost are still challenging, limiting their practical applications.
The available nitrate sensing devices have opted majorly two techniques, either colorimetric detection10 or ion-selective electrode (ISE) 11. Though the techniques are useful, but suffer from some major drawbacks. Devices based on ISE, use ionophores which suffer from major interference effects. As ionophores used in ISE relies on selective ion exchange that depends on size and charge of ion. Nitrate ionophores are designed to attract negatively charged monovalent ions, it means ions like chloride (Cl-), bromide (Br-) and perchlorate (ClO4-) along with nitrate can interact with the ionophores due to their comparable size leading to considerable interference effect. Also, the linearity concentration range is low, and the limit of detection (LOD) is quite high for ISE. Regular maintenance is needed for ISE by doing frequent calibration and the device is itself quite costly compared to other techniques. On the other hand, colorimetric kit-based devices for nitrate ion detection are very popular due to their cost-effective and rapid detection time. However, colorimetric test kits typically exhibit lower sensitivity compared to electrochemical sensors. This lower sensitivity may hinder the detection of trace nitrate ion levels and quantifying the exact concentration is frequently challenging due to the restricted visual range for color comparison which gives concentration values qualitatively. This limitation complicates the acquisition of accurate and consistent results in contrast to the quantitative measurements by electrochemical sensors. Additionally, several literatures on electrochemical sensing of nitrate ion are reported which majorly utilizes different polymers, metal nanoparticles and their nanocomposites. Works based on Cu nanoparticles are quite popular for nitrate ion sensing. Cu Micro-flowers for electrochemical sensing of nitrate ion in water have been reported12, but majorly suffers from storage stability issue and up to 3 days only the stability data is shown. This happens due to the rapid oxidation of Cu (0) nanoparticles into Cu(+1) and Cu(+2) states. Similarly, Cu-reduced graphene oxide (rGO) composite shows a drop in current response by 20 % within a week of storage. Other than Cu, Nickel oxide (Ni2O3)-rGO composites have been reported for nitrate ion sensing13, but it needs further complex modification by employing the use of ion-selective membrane coating over Ni2O3. So, it results in higher LOD value and major interference effect caused by Zn2+, Na+, Ca2+, SO42-. Electrodeposited Ag dendrites over laser induced graphene (LIG) surface are reported14, but compared to Cu, Ag shows lesser catalytic property for nitrate ion due to limited electron transfer efficiency and also electrodeposition of Ag over rough surface lacks the uniformity and homogeneity of the material over sensor surface which will affect the reproducibility of the sensor. The sensor showed almost 90% retention in current response upto 20 days of storage. Lastly, smart nitrate sensors are also reported based on ion imprinted polymer (IP) modified on interdigitated electrodes employing the impedance spectroscopy technique (EIS) 15. However, IP based sensors suffer from fouling effect and blocking of binding sites due to irreversible nature of binding of nitrate or other interfering ions. Though they rely on specific binding but fails to provide same level of amplification in signal as Cu nanoparticles. Hence, most of the non-enzymatic electrochemical nitrate sensing works reported in literature involve complex material fabrication steps, storage stability issues, complex data interpretation steps and limited practical application for onsite field testing.

There are a few commercial nitrate sensors available in market which basically runs on two major techniques, either colorimetric sensing strategy or ion selective electrode. LaMotte nitrate test kit functions16 on colorimetric detection technique which is also available on amazon. But this type sensors provides only qualitative concentration range, and doesn’t quantify the exact values present in real samples. Along with that color comparison (same color with different intensity) by naked eye can be challenging for common people. On the other hand, Hanna instruments H1982917 tester and LAQUA twin nitrate meter18 functions on ion selective membrane strategy. These sensors are very costly and also suffers from interference effect and the ion selective electrode degrades over time. Also, it requires frequent calibration for maintaining accuracy.
Some patents also reported based on nitrate sensor development which includes; Nitrate bio-electrochemical detection sensor driven by In2O3/In2S3 photo-anode and detection method (CN118671322A19). But due to the usage of biological components (Shewanella oneidensis MR-1), controlled conditions for the sensor are required and complex fabrication of In₂O₃/In₂S₃ heterojunction limits its scalability and reproducibility. Another, fluorescence based biosensors for measuring nitrate is reported (US20030232322A120) which suffers from limited practical applicability in complex, turbid, or highly contaminated samples where fluorescence signals can be quenched. Also, an in situ soil nitrate ion concentration sensor is reported (US7927883B221) which may result in inconsistency in ionic concentration measurement due to variability of soil comparison and moisture content that will affect the equilibrium process. Other than that, insertion of the probe and plunger displacement may introduce contaminants, altering the ionic composition of the sample and also ion selective electrodes are prone to signal drift leading to frequent recalibration for accurate results. Lastly, colorimetric determination of aqueous nitrate concentration is also reported (US20180031535 A122) which relies on indirect measurement that measures nitrite concentration and correlates it to nitrate, introducing potential errors, if in case the nitrate to nitrite conversion is incomplete. Not only that, it has sensitivity issues which is not suitable for very low nitrate concentration and reliance on specific water soluble thio-ether compounds increases the complexity and cost of the reagents.

Traversing the prior arts, it was learned that excessive use of nitrogen-containing fertilizers contaminates groundwater and surface water with nitrate ions, posing risks to human health, such as methemoglobinemia and carcinogenic compound formation. Monitoring nitrate levels is essential for soil and water quality. However, traditional methods like UV-VIS spectroscopy, ion chromatography, and enzymatic assays require bulky equipment, skilled operators, and pre-processing, making them unsuitable for on-site applications. While other techniques like colorimetric detection, ion-selective electrodes (ISE), and impedance spectroscopy (EIS) offer alternatives, they suffer from limitations such as low sensitivity, interference, high detection limits, and interference to environmental artifacts. Existing electrochemical sensors are also prone to material instability and reproducibility issues.
Hence, the proposed sensor surpasses existing technologies by combining allylamine-capped CuNPs and fCNT to achieve high sensitivity, stability, and reproducibility. Its use of Au-sputtered electrodes with laser-cut designs ensures scalable, low-cost production. The integration with smartphone facilitates real-time, on-site monitoring without complex instrumentation, making it a user-friendly and field-deployable solution.

OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION
The primary objective of the present invention is to develop a portable, non-enzymatic nitrate sensor system using strip-based electrodes integrated with a smart phone via pocket potentiostat for real-time detection addressing the shortcomings of traditional methods and enabling on-site, rapid, and cost-effective nitrate monitoring.

Another objective of the present invention is to fabricate the sensor system employing allylamine-capped Cu nanoparticles (Alym@CuNPs) for enhanced oxidation resistance, functionalized carbon nanotubes (fCNT) for improved electron transfer, and Au-sputtered strip electrodes (AuSE) with a uniform 100 nm layer to enhance catalytic activity along with a laser cutting process ensuring precise, low-cost electrode designs while a simplified filtration setup eliminates complex pre-processing steps.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION WITH REFERENCE TO THE ACCOMPANYING FIGURES:
Nitrate ion contamination of water is a major issue that affects many parts of the world due to excessive usage of nitrogen-containing fertilizers in soil. Thus, it is evident that nitrate ion monitoring in water and soil is an area of significant technological importance. High levels of nitrate ions are also damaging to human health since they are transformed into several dangerous nitrogen-based substances, including N-nitroso compounds, nitrite, and nitric oxide, which are linked to cancer, Parkinson's disease, acute respiratory tract infection, and gastritis. Most importantly, nitrate ions are responsible for methemoglobinemia or blue baby syndrome which occurs due to oxidation of the Fe2+ active center of hemoglobin into Fe3+ active center of methemoglobin by nitrate ions with a decreased oxygen transport capability. In the context of this, it is clear that creating a reliable, robust, portable and user-friendly device for the detection of nitrate ions is essential which can support ongoing efforts to monitor the agricultural soil health and drinkable quality of water. Since electrochemical sensors are quick, cost-effective, simple to use, and compatible with small and simple instruments, they are potentially suitable to overcome all of these limitations. Herein, we report the development of a non-enzymatic electrochemical nitrate sensing device comprising of mass-producible, stable, portable strip-based electrodes integrated seamlessly with smartphone via a pocket potentiostat for rapid and onsite sensing of nitrate ion from soil and water. As Cu nanoparticles function as an efficient catalytic material for nitrate ion sensing and also has a natural tendency to oxidise in the presence of aerial oxygen, hence most of the reported nitrate sensors suffer from poor stability. In this work, allylamine capped Cu nanoparticles-fCNT (Alym@CuNPs-fCNT) composite is used modified on Au sputtered strip electrode (AuSE) for nitrate ion sensing. So here, allylamine acts as a capping agent to protect the Cu from aerial oxidation along with that the presence of fCNT facilitates a greater electron transfer rate consequently increasing the sensitivity of the sensor and also ensuring homogenous dispersion of the material making the sensor surface highly reproducible. The AuSE functions as an excellent platform for the synthesized material due to its planarity and highly conductive nature which will enhance the catalytic property of the material to function properly for nitrate ion detection. The sputtering technique is employed for ultrathin (100 nm range) and uniform Au layer formation on polymeric substrates. Along with that, a laser cutting strategy is used to get the final design of the electrodes which replaces the usage of complex mask fabrication procedures and reduces the effective cost of each Au electrode strip. The AuSE modified with Alym@CuNps-fCNT (AuSE/Alym@CuNps-fCNT) composite shows storage stability up to 75 days with 95.0% retention in current value which is much higher compared to the reported works. And shows the LOD of 4.69 μM (n=3) which eventually after dilution of real sample satisfies the crucial required range of nitrate ion generally present in the water and soil samples  Reproducibility and repeatability studies of the sensing device yielded very low relative standard deviation (RSD) values of 0.72% and 0.70% respectively. Furthermore, electrochemical differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) studies have confirmed that the proposed sensing device can be reused even up to 6 times for different samples which makes the sensor cost-effective, and user-friendly. Additionally, the simple filtration setup for filtering out the soil sample and water samples replaces the usage of costly syringe filters available in the market and also replaces centrifugation and conventional filtration procedures performed in laboratory setups. Hence, this non-enzymatic nitrate sensing device developed here demonstrates very high storage stability, high reproducibility, high sensitivity, usage of a user-friendly and cost-effective setup. Along with that, it ensures rapid detection time (<5 min), good reusability up to 6 different samples and also demonstrates excellent percentage recovery characteristics (>92%) when compared to the gold standard method.

EXAMPLE 1

Synthesis of sensing material: Wet chemical synthesis of allylamine capped nanoparticles-functionalized multiwalled carbon nanotube composite (Alym@CuNPs-fCNT composite)

Initially 0.2 mg/mL of COOH functionalized multiwalled carbon nanotube (fCNT) was probe sonicated (UP100H, Hielscher) in DI type 1 water medium utilizing a horn-type probe for 60 minutes (0.5 cycle) at 35% amplitude. Parallelly CuSO4 (2 g) and 20 ml of type 1 deionized water (DI type 1) were added to a 50 ml conical flask and maintained at 600 rpm. Using an addition funnel, 2 ml of glycerine was added, and after 3 minutes of stirring 4 ml of allylamine was immediately added, and stirring continued for 30 minutes. Followed by that, the probe sonicated homogenous fCNT solution was added into the reaction medium and kept for stirring for 15 minutes. Lastly, 4 ml of hydrazine was added dropwise, stirring and maintaining the temperature for 30 minutes more, then kept for 30 mins at room temperature to cool it down. After this treatment, centrifugation at 12,000 rpm was used to retrieve the composite and washed two times with ethanol and DI type 1 water. The supernatant was finally discarded and residue composite were kept at hot air oven for 2 hours maintaining 60 degrees Celsius. The dried composite were obtained as a dark-brown coloured powder and labelled as allylamine capped copper nanoparticles-functionalized multiwalled carbon nanotubes composite (Alym@CuNPs-fCNT composite) illustrated in Fig. 1

 EXAMPLE 6

Details procedure of extraction of the real samples and working of the sensing device 

 For Soil sample 

1. Sample Preparation:

• Collect 5 g of soil (up to the 5 mL mark) in the Falcon tube provided in the kit
• Add 25 mL of acidic Na₂SO₄ electrolyte to the soil sample (supplied in the kit)

2. Shaking and Settling:

• Shake the tube vigorously for 5 minutes
• Let it stand vertically for 5 minutes to allow the soil particles to settle

3. Filtration:

• Use the plastic dropper to take a few mL of the supernatant.
• Filter the supernatant using Whatman filter paper and collect 0.5 mL of the filtrate in a small tube

4. Dilution:

• Add 2.5 mL of electrolyte to the 0.5 mL filtrate (30x dilution).

5. Electrochemical Measurement:

• Drop 0.1 mL of electrolyte on the sensor surface for a blank reading.
• Remove the blank solution, then add 0.1 mL of the diluted sample on the sensor surface for nitrate analysis.
• The data obtained will be in current value that will be matched with the calibration plot to get the exact nitrate ion concentration present in the soil sample 

 For Water sample 

1. Sample Preparation:

• Collect 5 mL of water (up to the 5 mL mark) in the Falcon tube provided in the kit
• Add 20 mL of acidic Na₂SO₄ electrolyte to the soil sample (supplied in the kit)

2. Filtration:

• Shake the solution and filter using the Whatman filter paper provided, then collect 1 mL of the filtrate in a small tube

3. Dilution:

• Add 1 mL of Na₂SO₄ electrolyte to the 1 mL filtrate (10x dilution)

4. Electrochemical Measurement:

• Drop 0.1 mL of electrolyte on the sensor surface for a blank reading.
• Remove the blank solution, then add 0.1 mL of the diluted sample on the sensor surface for nitrate analysis.
• The data obtained will be in current value that will be matched with the calibration plot to get the exact nitrate ion concentration present in the water sample

The term “microemulsion” refers to a thermodynamically stable, isotropic, and transparent (or translucent) mixture of oil, water, surfactants, and co-surfactants, typically having droplet sizes in the range of 10–100 nm. 
The term “gel” refers to a semi-solid system consisting of a network of polymers that may entrap the microemulsion, providing structural integrity and facilitating controlled release of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API). 
The term “microemulsion based / loaded gel” refers to a pharmaceutical or cosmetic preparation where a microemulsion is integrated into a gel matrix to enhance stability, bioavailability, or therapeutic efficacy.
The term “surfactant” refers to a compound that reduces surface tension and stabilizes the interface between the oil and water phases in the microemulsion system.
The term “Co-Surfactant” refers to a secondary surfactant used in combination with a primary surfactant to further reduce interfacial tension and promote the formation of microemulsions.

The term “Oil Phase” refers to the hydrophobic component of the microemulsion, typically consisting of oils or lipophilic substances, used to solubilize lipophilic drugs or enhance permeability.
The term “Aqueous Phase” refers to the hydrophilic component of the microemulsion, usually comprising water or water-miscible solvents.
The term “Droplet Size” refers to the diameter of the dispersed phase (oil or water droplets) in the microemulsion, typically measured in nanometers, which impacts stability, drug release, and absorption.
The term “Hydrophilic-Lipophilic Balance (HLB)” refers to a measure of the relative hydrophilicity or lipophilicity of a surfactant, influencing the type and stability of the microemulsion.
The term “Thermodynamic Stability” refers to a characteristic of the microemulsion system, indicating that it forms spontaneously without the need for external energy input, and remains stable over time.
The term “Viscosity” refers to the measure of the gel's resistance to flow, influenced by the polymer network and interaction with the microemulsion components.
The term “Bioavailability” relates to the extent and rate at which the API is absorbed into systemic circulation and becomes available at the intended site of action.
The term “Excipient(s)” refers to inactive components of the formulation that aid in stabilization, compatibility, or enhancement of drug delivery, such as thickeners, stabilizers, and penetration enhancers.

Natural plant extracts like Glycyrrhetinic acid have great potential for promoting wound healing and addressing various health issues. However, their clinical use is limited due to challenges with solubility, absorption, and bioavailability. Microemulsion systems present an effective solution to these challenges, improving the delivery and therapeutic effects of hesperidin. By enhancing its solubility and facilitating controlled, targeted release, microemulsions offer a promising approach to ameliorating treatments for skin conditions.

Example 1: Selection of oil, surfactant, and co-surfactant based on solubility properties 
The components selected for the ME formulation were pharmaceutically acceptable, non-irritating, and classified as GRAS (Generally Recognized as Safe). Among the oils tested, GA showed solubility in Arachis oil, with a value of 22.1±0.12 mg/ml as illustrated in Figure, and glyceryl monolinoleate  (Brand name:  maisine) (4.2±0.65 mg/ml) was also utilized in the oil phase. For surfactants, polyoxyethylene sorbitan monooleate 80 (Brand name: Tween 80) (18.56±0.22 mg/ml) and polyoxyl 35 hydrogenated castor oil ween (Brand name: Cremphor EL) (0.12±0.09 mg/ml), both non-ionic surfactants with HLB values of 14 and 12 respectively, exhibited excellent solubilizing properties, enhancing both solubility and bioavailability of the drug. Ethanol (0.612±0.11 mg/ml) was selected as the co-surfactant, demonstrating the highest solubility due to its ability to improve interfacial flexibility, facilitating the formation of stable, clear ME. The solubility of GA in different oils, surfactants and co-surfactants is summarized in Figure 1.

Example 2: Selection of concentration ranges of components used 
Selecting an appropriate oil-to-Smix ratio was crucial for developing an efficient ME. Pseudo-ternary phase diagrams were utilized to identify the ME region and establish the concentration ranges that maximize the ME area. These diagrams were constructed using Arachis oil, Maisine, Tween 80, Cremophor EL, Ethanol and distilled water. Phase transitions were monitored visually by observing changes in sample appearance, transitioning between turbid and clear states. The diagrams outlined an isotropic, low-viscosity region representing multiphase emulsions, while the single-phase microemulsion zone was identified separately. The ME region was notably larger with a 2:1 Smix ratio compared to a 1:1 ratio. The phase study revealed that the 2:1 ratio produced the most extensive ME area, making it the optimal choice for further development, as illustrated in Figure 2. 
Pseudo-ternary phase diagrams were developed by mixing oil and Smix in nine different ratios (9:1, 8:2, 7:3, 6:4, 5:5, 4:6, 3:7, 2:8, 1:9 %w/w) to identify the ME region, as shown in Figure. Among the tested Smix ratios, the 2:1 ratio produced the largest ME area. The 2:8 oil-to-Smix ratio resulted in a formulation with good transparency and a slight blue tint, characterized by a small globule size of 24.1±1.98 nm, a PDI value of 0.245±0.051, and a zeta potential of -6.065±0.32 mV. In comparison, the 1:9 oil-to-Smix ratio yielded an even smaller globule size of 18.34±2.87 nm and a lower PDI value of 0.197±0.043, likely due to higher Smix content. However, achieving a transparent ME required a much larger volume of the aqueous phase, which could displace oil droplets into the aqueous phase, causing an increase in globule size and instability after 12 hours. Other ratios (from 9:1 to 3:7) appeared turbid with larger globule sizes as shown in Figure 3
Thus, the 2:8 oil-to-Smix ratio, consisting of  2% oil (Arachis oil and Maisine), 8% surfactant Smix (with equal amounts of Tween 80, Cremophor EL and PEG-400 in a 2:1 ratio), and 90% distilled water, was selected as the final formulation for the GA-ME, and GA-MEG, and various characterization parameters were evaluated. 
Example 3: Glycyrrhetinic acid Loaded Microemulsion formation and characterisation. 
The glycyrrhetinic acid-loaded microemulsion (GA-ME) was formulated using the titration method. GA was initially dissolved in the oil phase (Archais oil and Maisine), followed by the preparation of the optimised Smix ratio. In the 2:1 Smix ratio, Tween 80 and Cremophor EL constituted equal parts of the “2” portion (1:1), while ethanol made up the “1” portion. The components were mixed thoroughly using a magnetic stirrer, and distilled water was added gradually while stirring until a clear and uniform oil-in-water (o/w) ME was achieved. The formulation was fine-tuned by adjusting the proportions of oil, surfactant, co-surfactant and water, along with optimising process parameters such as stirring speed and duration. 
Various Characterization parameters of GA-ME were performed, and the results are tabulated in Table 1 
The average globule size of the GA-ME was found to be 25.9±2.18 nm, with a PDI of 0.265±0.051 as shown in Figure 3  indicating a relatively narrow distribution of particle sizes. The zeta potential of the formulation was recorded at -6.065±0.32 mV. The negative zeta potential is primarily due to the characteristics of the drug molecule itself, while the use of non-ionic surfactants and co-surfactants in the formulation also contributed to this property.
The % transmittance of GA-ME was assessed by diluting the formulation 100 times with 0.1N HCl and measuring at 650 nm, yielding a value of 86.34±1.23. the transmittance values confirmed the microemulsion’s optical clarity, transparency, and stability, which are crucial for its efficacy.
The pH of the GA-ME was measured at 5.87±1.78, whereas the formulation without the drug had a pH of 6.13±1.43. these values suggest that the formulation is well-suited for use on human skin.
Viscosity is an important factor in topical delivery as it affects how long the product stays on the skin. When the dispersed phase volume fraction is low, the ME typically contains nanosized droplets that have minimal interaction, leading to low viscosity. The observed low viscosity in this formulation was also due to its lower content. The viscosity of the GA-ME, measured at 100 rpm, was determined to be 8.12±1.76 cP.
The drug content analysis showed an entrapment efficiency of 96.34±1.21%, demonstrating that the drug was successfully encapsulated within the microemulsion.

Example 4: Preparation of Hesperidin-loaded microemulsion gel (H-MEG)

Konjac glucomannan (KG) gels with concentrations of 0.1%, 0.5%, 1%, and 1.5% were prepared in distilled water using a magnetic stirrer . The 0.1%, 1%, and 1.5% KG gels had viscosities that were either too low or too high, making them unsuitable for topical application. Therefore, 0.5% KG was mixed with C940 in concentrations of 0.5%, 0.75%, and 1%, and the mixtures were tested for viscosity using a viscometer at 50, 60, and 100 rpm. The mixture of 0.5% KG and 1% C940 demonstrated ideal rheological properties for efficient topical drug delivery as described in the various characterization parameters. The GA-ME was further added to the optimised KGC gel to make GA-MEG. 
The formulation was clear, viscous, and had a smooth consistency. Its pH ranged from 5.91± 0.1, and the viscosity measured at 50 rpm was 6230±50 cP. The drug content range was found to be 94.47±0.27%.
Spreadability is an essential characteristic of gel formulations, as it allows for easy application to inflamed areas with minimal drag and optimal slip. When a measured amount of gel was placed between two glass plates of known weight, it spread evenly to form a circular shape. The diameter of this circle was directly proportional to the gel’s Spreadability. The larger the diameter, the better the Spreadability. The diameter of the GA-MEG was found to be 7.1±0.4cm.

Example 5: In-vitro release study 
The drug release behaviour of both GA-ME and GA-MEG was assessed using a Franz diffusion cell. Hydrated cellulose acetate membranes were placed between the donor and receptor compartments. The receptor chamber, filled with phosphate buffer at pH 7.4 was kept at a constant temperature of 37±1°C throughout the experiment. The cumulative drug release was calculated and plotted against time, as shown in Figure 4. The GA-ME formulation releases 95.4±1.45% of the drug within 24 hours, indicating a relatively rapid yet sustained release. On the other hand, The GA-MEG formulation releases 61.9±1.87% of the drug over the same period, demonstrating a slower, more controlled release. Both formulations effectively provided sustained drug release, with the gel-based GA-MEG offering a more gradual release, making it ideal for prolonged therapeutic effects
Example 6: Ex-vivo diffusion study
An ex-vivo diffusion study was conducted to compare the release profiles of GA-ME and GA-MEG formulations using pig ear skin. The drug was applied topically, and diffusion was monitored over 24 hours. The results showed that GA-ME facilitated 84.9±1.67% drug diffusion through the skin within 24 hours, while GA-,MEG demonstrated a slower release, with 55.8±1.87% diffusion over the same period, as depicted in Figure 5. the cumulative drug release data confirmed sustained drug delivery for both formulations, with GA-MEG exhibiting a more gradual and controlled permeation compared to the faster release from GA-ME. The receptor chamber was kept at 37±1°C, using physiological saline (pH 5.5) as the medium, and stirred at 50 rpm to simulate in-vivo conditions for topical application. These findings suggest that while GA-ME provides effective sustained drug diffusion, GA-MEG offers better control and prolonged skin retention, making it a preferable option for extended therapeutic action.

For purposes of the present invention, the terms "active agent", "drug" , “active” “bioactive” “medicament” “active pharmaceutical ingredient”  are used interchangeably, and are meant to encompass a single essential oil contained in the topical spray formulations of the invention.
The term "efficacy" as used herein refers to the extent to which a treatment produces a beneficial result, e.g., an improvement in one or more symptoms of the disease. In one embodiment, efficacy is evaluated by lesion counting, which is a current practice to assess severity of acne.
A "therapeutically effective amount" means the amount that, when administered to an animal for treating a disease, is sufficient to effect treatment for that disease.
The term "stable" refers to a minimal change in physical and chemical properties of the composition over time relative to when it is manufactured. Stability over time may be evaluated based on pre-defined criteria including assay of active and related compounds, appearance, color, and pH.
The term “Thermodynamic Stability” refers to a characteristic of the microemulsion system, indicating that it forms spontaneously without the need for external energy input, and remains stable over time.
The term “Bioavailability” relates to the extent and rate at which the API is absorbed into systemic circulation and becomes available at the intended site of action.
The term “cocrystal”, as used herein refers to a crystalline phase wherein at least two components of the crystal interact by hydrogen bonding or other non-covalent interactions but not by ion pairing. A cocrystal is only formed when the adhesive interactions overcome the size/shape mismatch features of the parent molecules to form a distinct and specific crystal lattice that is inherently thermodynamically stable.
The term “cocrystal former”, as used herein refers to a compound which interacts with the main component, e.g. a pharmaceutically active compound of the cocrystal by non-covalent interactions such as hydrogen bonding.
The term “cocrystal of Lafutidine”, as used herein refers to a supramolecular structure of Lafutidine wherein the Lafutidine molecule is hydrogen bonded to a cocrystal former without altering the chemical structure of Lafutidine.
Although any methods similar or equivalent to those described herein can be used in the practice or testing of embodiments of the present disclosure, the exemplary methods are now described. The described embodiments are merely exemplary of the disclosure, which may be embodied in various forms.
Various modifications to the embodiment will be readily apparent to those skilled in the art and the generic principles herein may be applied to other embodiments. However, one of ordinary skill in the art will readily recognize that the present disclosure is not intended to be limited to the embodiments illustrated, but is to be accorded the widest scope consistent with the principles and features described herein.

? The formation of cocrystals is a green chemistry approach where catalytic amount (minimum) of solvent is used for their synthesis. 
? The crystal engineering technique aims at rapid cocrystal development through synthon approach which improves API physicochemical properties without affecting its intrinsic structure and function.
? The alterations are made in the crystal lattice of the cocrystal through non-covalent interactions. No breaking or formation of covalent bonds is involved.
? The cocrystals synthesis is carried out at ambient temperatures (higher temperatures are not required) easily scalable and results in product of high purity.
EXAMPLES
The invention is illustrated by the following examples which are only meant to illustrate the invention and not to act as limitations. All embodiments apparent to a process there in the art are deemed to fall within the scope of the present invention. 
Example 1: Characterisation of Co-crystals
The prepared co-crystals of Formula 3 have been characterised using various techniques as given below: 
Thermal analysis 
The DSC analysis was carried out to study the thermal behaviour of lafutidine cocrystals in comparison to pure drug lafutidine and glycine conformer as presented in fig. 1. These are significantly different from the melting endotherm of lafutdine co-crystals. 
Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves of pure lafutidine and glycine show sharp endothermic peaks at 101.35 ?C and 233.34 ?C respectively. The co-crystals (3) showed a single endotherm at 184.87 ?C when lafutidine and glycine are taken in the ratio of 1:1. 
The melting of the product at 184.87 ?C is in between the melting of drug and co-former suggesting the formation of a cocrystal. 
Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy 
FT-IR is an analytical technique which provides molecular level information. The interaction amongst the functional groups of coformer and parent drug is revealed by shifts in characteristic peaks depicted. The changes in the peak position in FTIR spectra are also indicative of the changes in the interaction between the drug and coformer. 
Furthermore, the PXRD analysis of product formed shows appearance of novel peaks, as compared to pure lafutidine and glycine, suggesting the development of new crystal lattice. 
Equilibrium solubility studies 
Solubility of cocrystals of lafutidine  was determined in phosphate buffer (pH 6.8) and 0.1 N HCl (pH 1.2) at 37°C . The quantitative analysis was done using HPLC. The results were found to be significant when compared by One-way ANOVA using GraphPad Prism  software at 95% confidence interval. The equilibrium solubility was also determined for cocrystal and an increase of 2.4 folds was observed. 
Intrinsic Dissolution Studies 
Intrinsic dissolution studies of Lafutidine and its cocrystals were performed in phosphate buffer (pH 6.8) and 0.1 N HCl (pH 1.2) at 37°C using HPLC. Additionally, an intrinsic dissolution rate study was also determined which gave the cumulative drug release. It was also found that the drug's intrinsic dissolving rate was increased when it was present in the cocrystal.
