Description:DETAILED DESCRIPTION   
[0017] This disclosure provides a transdermal delivery system designed for the controlled and sustained delivery of a therapeutic agent, specifically SB202190, which may inhibit neuroinflammatory pathways and ameliorate neurobehavioral disorders. The system can include a solvent, such as ethanol, in which the therapeutic agent is dissolved. A polymer base may be mixed with the solvent and therapeutic agent to form a uniform matrix. This matrix can be spread onto a backing layer, typically a polyester film, and dried to form a patch. An adhesive layer and a release liner may be added to complete the patch structure. The patch can be cut into desired sizes and packaged in moisture-proof and light-resistant materials, such as aluminum foil, to ensure stability. The transdermal patch may incorporate permeation enhancers, stabilizers, and biocompatible materials to ensure the efficacy and stability of the therapeutic agent. The patch facilitates the controlled release of SB202190 into the bloodstream through the skin, potentially reducing neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby mitigating symptoms of anxiety, depression, and cognitive impairment.  
[0018] In an embodiment, polymer base can be hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), ethyl cellulose (EC), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), polyacrylate polymers, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), chitosan.
[0019] In yet other embodiment, adhesive layer can be silicone-based adhesives, acrylic adhesives, polyisobutylene adhesives, polyurethane adhesives or pressure-sensitive adhesives (PSAs).
[0020] In a further embodiment, release liner can be silicone coatings, polyethylene (PE), polyester (PET), fluoropolymer coatings or paper backing.

Abstract:
Abstract:

The invention relates to a method for preparing a hydroethanolic extract of green coffee Arabica beans. The process involves extracting coarse powder of the beans with a hydroalcoholic solvent, followed by distillation to remove the solvent and drying the resultant semi-solid product. The extract is then stored under specific conditions and dissolved for in vitro assays. The extract contains bioactive compounds such as chlorogenic acid and trigonelline, exhibits antioxidant activity, and has potential therapeutic applications. Additionally, an oral syrup composition containing the extract is formulated for therapeutic use, with ingredients selected to enhance stability, palatability, and visual appeal. Reference Fig 1

[0021] Examples: 
Example 1: Extraction procedure
The shade dried beans of green coffee Arabica were powdered and passed via a sieve of 40 mesh size. The coarse powder was put through the Soxhlet apparatus and extraction was done for 12 hours at 70°C by subjecting 1.5 kg of the drug to ethanol and water (70:30 v/v). The suspension was filtered through Whatman no. 4 filter paper. The resulting hydroethanolic solutions were exposed to distillation to remove the solvent at a temperature of 60°C using a rotary evaporator. The semi-solid product obtained after distillation was dried in a vacuum desiccator and its properties and yield were recorded. The extract was stored at 4°C in a refrigerator. Further, to assess in vitro assays, this extract was dissolved in solvent.
Example 2: Preliminary Phytochemical Screening 
To carry out the phytochemical screening of the active phytoconstituents present in hydroethanolic extract of green coffee beans, standard protocol was followed.
HPTLC Quantification of Chlorogenic acid and Trigonelline in GCBE extract  
The obtained extract was subjected to HPTLC analysis for quantitative determination of chlorogenic acid and trigonelline. Before moving HPTLC first optimization of solvent system for the GCBE was done by using precoated silica gel GF254. HPTLC quantification was used to confirm the presence of chlorogenic acid and trigonelline in extract through Rf determination and compared with standard.
Total phenolics estimation
Total phenolic content of extracts was determined using Folin Ciocalteu reagent. 10 mg of the extract was mixed with 10 ml of methanol (1 mg/ml). 0.4 ml of this extract was taken and mixed separately with 2 ml of Folin-Ciocalt reagent and 1.6 ml of sodium carbonate. Let the reaction mixture to stand for 2 h and record the absorbance at 750 nm. All measurements were made in triplicate. 
Total flavonoids estimation
The extent of total flavonoids was determined by aluminium chloride colorimetry method. 1 mg/ml solution was prepared by dissolving 10 mg of the extract in 10 ml of methanol. 0.5 ml of this extract was taken out and dissolved in1 ml of 10% aluminium chloride, 0.1 ml of 1 M potassium acetate, 1.5 ml of methanol, and 2.8 ml of distilled water. The mixture was incubate for 30 min at room temperature and at 415nm, the absorbance was recorded. All measurements were accomplished in triplicate. 
Example 3: Antioxidant activity
In vitro antioxidant activity of the extract was investigated using standard methods such as DPPH (2, 2-Diphenyl-1-picryl-hydrazyl) test, ABTS Scavenging Test, Nitric oxide radical assay, Superoxide radical assay.

Example 8: The Impact of EPHAE (50, 100, 150 mg/kg) on kidney and liver histology in NAD-STZ-induced DN.
Histological study of kidney tissue (Figure 6) from various experimental groups indicated significant changes in renal architecture. In the vehicle control, medium treatment, high treatment and standard treatment groups, the kidney tissues were found to be healthy, with no evidence of degradation, swelling and well-preserved Bowman's capsules. In contrast, the disease control group showed significant pathological abnormalities, including swelling of the renal tubules, which is indicative of early-stage tubular degeneration. A similar, albeit less prominent, degree of swelling was detected in the low-treatment group, indicating a partial reduction in disease impact compared to the control group. Active ingredient
The term “active ingredient” of the present invention is used to denote a Non-steroidal anti inflammatory drug (NSAID) particularly etodolac. 
Etodolac, chemically known as (±)-1,8-diethyl-1,3,4,9-tetrahydropyrano[3,4-b]indole-1-acetic acid, is a white crystalline compound that is insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents like ethanol and methanol. Its molecular formula is C17H21NO3 and it has a molecular weight of 287.35 g/mol. 
Etodolac is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) commonly used to relieve pain and reduce inflammation in conditions like arthritis. It works by inhibiting the production of certain chemicals in the body that cause inflammation and pain.
Etodolac is classified as a BCS (Biopharmaceutics Classification System) Class II drug. This means it has low solubility and high permeability. In terms of solubility, etodolac is sparingly soluble in water, which can impact its dissolution and absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. This property may influence its bioavailability and pharmacokinetic profile when administered orally.
In an aspect of the embodiment, etodolac is used in a concentration of 10-20% w/w, preferably 15% w/w. 
Phospholipids 
Phospholipids play a crucial role in the formation and function of complexes , which are specialized lipid-based vesicles used in drug delivery systems. 
Phospholipids are a class of lipids that are major components of cell membranes. They consist of a glycerol molecule, two fatty acid chains, and a phosphate group. The phosphate group is typically linked to an alcohol molecule, such as choline, ethanolamine, or serine, forming various types of phospholipids like phosphatidylcholine, phosphatidylethanolamine, and phosphatidylserine. Phospholipids have a hydrophilic ("water-attracting") head and hydrophobic ("water-repelling") tails, which allow them to form bilayers in aqueous environments, creating the basic structure of cell membranes. They play essential roles in cell structure, signaling, and membrane integrity.
Further, the composition of phospholipids in the complexes influences its fluidity. Phospholipids with unsaturated fatty acid tails increase membrane fluidity, allowing complexes to deform and squeeze through narrow pores, such as those found in the skin's intercellular spaces, facilitating transdermal drug delivery. They also encapsulate the active ingredient within the aqueous core or lipid bilayers of transfersomes. This encapsulation protects the drug molecules from degradation and facilitates their transport to the target site.

Description:Field of the invention: 

The present invention relates to organic fertilizer. More specifically organic fertilizer made from silt collected at the bottom of specially curated ponds during summer and the process of making this. These ponds are enriched with organic materials like tree leaves, fish and bird excreta, and rainwater runoff, creating nutrient-rich silt layers. At the end of summer, the water is pumped out, and the silt is sun-dried for a week in the pond. The top nutrient-rich layer of silt is dredged and transported to paddy fields, where it is sun-dried again to form a semi-powdered, tilling-friendly fertilizer.

Background of the Invention

Silt, by definition, is rock, mineral or clay fragments 1/20 millimeter diameter or smaller. These tiny pieces of geologic wonder are easily moved by water flow and quick to settle once the movement stops, depositing itself in waves where the water slows.
Silt can have both positive and negative effects on a pond.
Positive effects: Silt can provide insulation for animals in the pond, and silty soil can be good for growing crops. Some silt can also be a source of nutrients for waterlilies whereas the negative effects includes reduced water quality, habitat disruption, increasing risk of flooding, loss of fish and wildlife along with bad odor and dense algae bloom. 

Present invention is about silt as a source of nutrients. Reference is invited for few of the relevant journal papers and patents which talk about organic fertilizer from pond silt, are mentioned hereinafter.

The analysis shows that PPS has significantly higher levels of organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and sulfur compared to regular rice field soil, making it an effective fertilizer. The cultivation of para grass using PPS proved to be more economically viable than rice production, benefiting small-scale dairy farming. Detailed Description of the Invention

As stated hereinbefore, the present invention relates to the preparation of organic fertilizer in a standalone way from pond silt, with high NPK content, which advantageously promotes high productivity in paddy cultivation while ensuring sustainable use of organic content. Advantageously present invention offers to get rid of the harmful effect of indiscriminate use of chemical fertilizer along with pesticides and herbicides in agricultural production process by employing organic fertilizers. Application of organic fertilizer in accordance to the present invention for agricultural production is extremely effective in improving the quality of soil, preserving the soil health, while producing high-yields of paddy with enriched nutrition.

There are various types of organic fertilizers available for paddy crops, and each has its own benefits and disadvantages. For example, a popular organic fertilizer, compost increases soil health and structure, is made from decomposed organic matter, such as leaves, grass clippings, and kitchen scraps. Compost also helps retain moisture in the soil, reducing the need for frequent watering.

Another organic fertilizer suitable for adding nitrogen to the soil is Fish emulsion which is made from fish waste and is rich in nitrogen. Fish emulsion is also an excellent source of micronutrients, such as calcium, magnesium, and sulfur.

Another popular organic fertilizer Bone meal is rich in phosphorus. It is made from crushed animal bones and is an excellent source of calcium, which is essential for strong root development. Bone meal also helps improve soil pH, making it more alkaline, which is beneficial for paddy crops.  (Farm Doktor: Reaping the Benefits of Organic Fertilizer for Paddy Crops, May 11, 2023) 

The organic fertilizer of the present application is comprised of leaves, fallen naturally in the pond, Fish excreta and other organic naturally produced floral and faunal materials (Flora comprises various types of plants, including trees, flowers, shrubs, and more. These plants interact with the environment, other organisms, and humans. Fauna encompasses a wide range of animal species, from insects and birds to mammals and reptiles). This selection of pond and the collection of an optimum layer of silt materials are done to ensure that the contents of the organic fertilizer become enriched with micronutrients. The ponds in the tropical region and the immediately adjoining sub-tropical regions are rich of natural vegetation and their leaves fall regularly to the ground and waterbodies nearby. Therefore, the right selection of ponds in the densely vegetated areas, along with a rich pisciculture practice of the local population brings out a unique composition of pond silt hitherto unexplored and came out only from rigorous study, experiments, and data collection through our field-based research, and not from a random selection.  It is worth mentioning here that none of the prior art has reported pond silt as a standalone way to produce a fertilizer to be used directly in the tilling process preferably for cultivation of paddy as disclosed for field  trials/experiments.  

For the present invention an organic fertilizer in semi powdered form with mild malodor is produced from the silt that is collected from the bottom of specialized curated ponds in the summer time. The ponds are first enriched with organic materials over a period of few months (6-8 months), involving addition of tree leaves, either falling naturally from the surrounding trees or otherwise, excreta from the fishes and birds that are allowed in the pond ecosystem, and also by allowing the runoff from the rainwater to bring organic matter from the nearby areas. The pond, in this case, leaves layers of content rich silt at the bottom of it, ranging several feet. 

The collection of the silt is carried out at the end of summer time when the water level is at its lowest, after pumping out the water till the silt gets visible at the bottom. Then, the silt is allowed to be sun-dried for a week in the pond itself, before it gets transported to the target paddy fields through dredging. Only a select layer of silt is dredged to ensure that the bottom silt is protected while the nutrient rich top layer is removed for further processing. The silt collected is again sun-dried in the paddy field for 10–14 days to transform it into a powdered form with uniform and tilling-friendly consistency before it is added to the tilling process. The resulting organic fertilizer is unique in its characteristics with sustainably high NPK content and proved to be pest/insect resistant for the paddy that gets cultivated, while also ensuring cyclical organic content usage along with high productivity of the paddy.


Example-1 
 
Collection of Organic Fertilizer
Based on few select criteria as disclosed below the ponds are undertaken for the present study. The ponds are enriched first with organic materials over a period of few months (6-8 months), involving addition of tree leaves, either falling naturally from the surrounding trees or otherwise, excreta from the fishes and birds that are allowed in the pond ecosystem, and also by allowing the runoff from the rainwater to bring organic matter from the nearby areas. The curated pond selected to extract organic manure (silt) (A pond in Bishnubati Mouza, Birbhum district, West Bengal) meets all these preconditions. 

The pond’s water was removed using pumps, and the silt was dried under sunlight for 7-10 days. Mini-excavators then dredged the dry silt, which was transported to sample fields. The silt collected is again sun-dried in the paddy field for 10-14 days to transform it into a powdered form with uniform and tilling-friendly consistency before it is added to the tilling process. Samples of fresh and dry silt were collected to determine the content of Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K) using the Kjeldahl method, Olsen/Bray method, and Flame photometer method, respectively. At the project site, the estimated N, P, and K content in dry pond silt samples were 150.52 kg/ha, 23.29 kg/ha, and 450.14 kg/ha, respectively. 

Drying of silt in the pond is done for two purposes: first, it gets easier to transport the silt from the pond to the agriculture field; and secondly, it helps in making accurate measurement of the NPK values of the silt in absence of water. Otherwise, the water will dilute the NPK content in the silt, and that in turn, will lead to errors in the measurement of the NPK value in the silt and further in the soil. In addition, the process of drying ensures nutrient retention and enrichment in the silt itself to enhance the quality of the output fertilizer.  



Field trials

The study was conducted on four paddy fields (S1, S2, S3, S4) totaling 20 Bighas (12.4 acres). Each field was treated with 500 cubic feet of dry pond silt per Bigha, amounting to 10,000 cubic feet for all fields.  The quantification of the silt per bigha was done to make an equivalence of the inorganic fertilizer that was previously being used and also to standardize the NPK content that would be contained in the soil required for paddy cultivation. We have not mixed silt arbitrarily, rather rigorous experimentation with different quantity of organic fertilizer it is observed that 500 CFT for a Bigha of land is sufficient to increase the N, P, and K level in the soil which is good enough for paddy cultivation. The amount is decided based on empirical research at the field level. The silt was dried for 10-14 days under sunlight on the agricultural field and then mixed evenly with the soil by manual labor. 

Farmers seeded the crops within 7-10 days, with rice seedlings planted in the first week of July 2023 and harvested in the first week of December 2023. A fifth field (S5), using chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and insecticides, was included for comparative analysis. Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to a spot welding device that is capable of providing a means to perform a spot welding on a workpiece by holding the workpiece in a stable manner and accordingly apply proper heating effect on the workpiece without affecting integrity structure of the workpiece in facilitating a strong and reliable bond between the workpiece.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002]  Spot welding on workpiece plays an important role in ensuring a strong and reliable bond between two metal surfaces. This process uses high levels of heat and pressure to create a secure connection, making it ideal for joining materials in automotive and manufacturing industries. One key advantage of spot welding is ability to produce consistent and precise welds quickly, increasing efficiency in production processes. Additionally, the minimal heat-affected zone helps to maintain the integrity of the surrounding material, reducing the risk of distortion or damage. Overall, spot welding is efficient method for creating strong bonds in metal fabrication for various applications in industries where precision and durability are essential. 

[0003] Traditionally the user uses tools for spot welding on the workpiece includes handheld welding guns, robotic welding arms, and resistance spot welding machines. These tools provide precise control over the welding process and ensure strong, reliable welds for various applications. However, advancements in technology have led to the development of more automated and efficient spot welding equipment, such as laser welding systems and automated robotic welding cells. These modern tools offer increased speed, accuracy, and consistency in spot welding operations but often requires proper skills in the field of welding techniques. 

[0004] CN202667903U discloses a utility model discloses a handheld spot welding machine which comprises a handheld part, wherein a pressure switch is arranged in the handheld part, two groups of springs connected with the pressure switch are arranged at the bottom of the handheld part and, lower portions of the springs are connected with two groups of welding needles, and end portions of the welding needles are provided with two groups of welding heads. An electric wire is led out through the handheld part and connected with a servo motor which supplies electricity to the welding heads. The handheld spot welding machine is simple in structure, spot welding can be carried out flexibly and conveniently, and the handheld spot welding machine can be broadly applied to a battery processing industry. Although, CN’903 provides way to assist the user in welding activity by using a servo motor which supplies electricity to the welding heads, however lacks in alerting the user regarding overheating of the workpiece during welding operation.

[0005] Conventionally, many devices are disclosed in prior art that provides way to allow a user to do spot welding over a workpiece but lacks in providing precise control over the welding parameter result in inconsistent weld quality and potentially compromised structural integrity of the workpiece. Moreover, such devices are lacks in applying proper heating effect over the workpiece due to which the workpiece gets affected due to overheating.

[0006] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of allow a user to do spot welding over a workpiece with precise control over the welding parameter without compromising structural integrity of the workpiece with proper heating effect over the workpiece.

[0021]  The proposed device comprises of a rectangular base 101 made up of any material selected from but not limited to metallic material and wooden material alike and encased with various component associated with the device arrange in sequential manner that aids in performing spot welding on a work piece. The base 101 is developed to position on a ground surface. Herein, a rigid inverted L-shaped member 105 having a rounded end, is attached with a rigid vertical structure 111 mounted on the base 101 for supporting a work piece for welding. Upon positioning the base 101 on the surface, the user requires to access a rectangular plate 103 assembled on the base 101 by means of a vertical actuator 104 for sitting and activate the device manually by pressing a switch button integrated on the base 101. The button is type of a switch that is internally connected with the device via multiple circuits that upon pressing by the user, the circuits get closed and starts conduction of electricity that tends to activate the device and vice versa. 

[0022] After activating of the device by the user, a microcontroller associated with the device generates a commands to operate the device accordingly. Upon activating the device, the microcontroller activates touch-enabled display unit 110 integrated with the structure 111 for giving access to the user for providing input commands regarding initiating or stopping the welding. The display unit 110 works by using LCD (liquid crystals) that are manipulated by electric currents to control the passage of light through the display. When an electric current is applied, the liquid crystals align in a way that either allows light to pass through or blocks it, creating the images and colors that is being visible in the LCD of the display unit 110 regarding the initiating or stopping the welding eight that is further change the electric charge at the location of the touch to register as input. The input is stored in the microcontroller to process the input.

[0023] Upon processing the input, the microcontroller activates a microphone 108 integrated in the structure 111 for giving voice commands regarding welding a work piece. The microphone 108 receives sound waves generated by energy emitted from the voice command in the form of vibrations. After then, the sound waves are transmitted towards a diaphragm configured with a coil. Upon transmitting the waves within the diaphragm, the diaphragm strikes with the waves due to which the coil starts moving the diaphragm with a back-and-forth movement in presence of magnetic field generated from the coil. After that the electric signal is emitted from the coil due to back-and-forth movement of the diaphragm which is further transmitted to a microcontroller linked with the microphone 108 to process the signal to analyze the signal for detecting voice command given by the user.

[0024]  Upon processing the voice commands, the microcontroller actuates an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 107 integrated in the structure 111 to determine orientation and shape of the work piece to be welded. The imaging unit 107, disclosed herein comprises of a camera and processor that works in collaboration to capture and process the images in a vicinity of the structure 111. The camera firstly captures multiple images of the vicinity of the structure 111, wherein the camera comprises of a body, electronic shutter, lens, lens aperture, image sensor, and imaging processor that works in sequential manner to capture images of the vicinity of the structure 111.

[0025]  After capturing of the images by the camera, the shutter is automatically open due to which the reflected beam of light coming from the surrounding due to light is directed towards the lens aperture. After then the reflected light beam passes through the image sensor. The sensor now analyzes the beam to retrieve signal from the beams which is further calibrate by the sensor to capture images of the vicinity of the structure 111 in electronic signal. Upon capturing images, the imaging processor processes the electronic signal into digital image. When the capturing is done, the processor associated with the imaging unit 107 processes the captured images by using a protocol of artificial intelligence to retrieve data from the captured image in the form of digital signal. The detected data is now transmitted to the microcontroller based on which the microcontroller acquires the data to detect the orientation and shape of the work piece to be welded. 

[0026] Based on detecting the orientation and shape of the work piece to be welded, the microcontroller generates commands to actuate a ball and socket joint integrated with a L-shaped telescopic link 106 attached with the structure 111 for providing movement to a conductive rounded tip fabricated with tip of the link 106 towards the work piece supported on the rounded end of the member 105. The ball and socket joint is a mechanical arrangement consists of a ball-shaped component that fits into a socket, with a motor providing the necessary power to drive the rotation to provide angular movement to the link 106 towards the work piece supported on the rounded end of the member 105.

[0027] Simultaneously, the microcontroller actuates a pneumatic unit integrated with the L-shaped telescopic link 106 to extend for making contact of the conductive rounded tip with the work piece supported on the rounded end of the member 105. The pneumatic unit comprises of an air compressor, air cylinder, air valves i.e. Inlet and outlet valve and piston that works in collaboration to aid extension and retraction of the link 106. The air compressor is coupled with a motor that gets activated by the microcontroller to compress the air from surroundings upon entering from the inlet valve to compressed and pumped out via the outlet valve. The air valve allows entry or exit of the compressed air from the compressor. Furthermore, the valve opens and the compressed air enters inside the cylinder thereby increasing the air pressure of the cylinder. The piston is connected to the cylinder and due to the increase in the air pressure, the piston extends. 

[0028] And upon closing of the valve, the compressed air exit out from the cylinder thereby decreasing the air pressure of the cylinder. The increasing and decreasing of the air pressure from the cylinder aids in extension and retraction of the piston that turns in aiding extension and retraction of the link 106 to position the rounded tip in contact with the work piece for welding by passage of electricity. After that the multiple suction cups provided on the rounded end of the member 105 create partial vacuum within the cups upon pressing over the workpiece by squeezing out air from the cups due to a negative pressure is generated inside suction area.

[0029] Upon generation of negative pressure, atmospheric pressure outside the cups presses down low-pressure area inside the cups to generate suction to adhere the workpiece to hold the work piece in a stable manner for welding by passage of electricity. Herein, the member 105 is made up of conductive material that passes electricity for welding the workpiece. A battery (not shown in figure) is associated with the device and connected with the rounded end of the member 105 and the rounded tip of the link 106 to facilitate an electric current for enabling welding. 

[0030] The battery discloses, herein offers power to the rounded end of the member 105 and the rounded tip of the link 106 necessary for their correct operation. The battery is linked to the microcontroller and provides (DC) Direct Current to the microcontroller. And then, based on the order of operations, the microcontroller sends that current to the rounded end of the member 105 and the rounded tip of the link 106. The battery operates by converting chemical energy into electrical energy, which is then used to generate heat at the rounded end of the member 105 and the rounded tip of the link 106 for melting the workpiece being welded together, creating a strong bond between the workpiece. 

[0031] During welding operation, a temperature sensor integrated in the member 105 detects a temperature of the workpiece. The temperature sensor is equipped with two electrodes utilized to detect the rise in voltage across the electrodes due to heating of the workpiece. The detecting voltage is equivalent to the temperature that is sensed by the sensor. After then the sensor converts that detected temperature into electric signals and transmits that signal into the microcontroller. After that the microcontroller processes and analyze the signal to detect the temperature of the workpiece. 

[0032] Based on detection of the workpiece’s temperature, if the detected temperature exceeds a threshold temperature pre-fed in database of the microcontroller, then the microcontroller actuates a speaker 109 provided on the base 101 to generate an audio alert regarding an overheating condition. The speaker 109 includes a diaphragm, which is typically made of a lightweight and rigid material like paper, plastic, or metal to vibrate and produce sound waves when electrical signals are fed to it for notifying the user. After passing of the electrical signal through a voice coil suspended within a magnetic gap of the speaker 109, it generates a magnetic field that interacts with the fixed magnetic field produced by a magnet assembly associated with the voice coil.

[0033] Upon variation in electrical current, the magnetic field produced by the voice coil changes, resulting in the voice coil and attached cone/diaphragm moving back and forth. This movement creates pressure variations in the surrounding air, generating sound waves to generate the audible sound to notify the user regarding an overheating condition of the workpiece. Additionally, a vacuum unit is integrated on the structure 111 for removal of welding fumes generated during welding. The vacuum unit comprises of an impeller configured with multiple vanes and which is directly coupled with the shaft of a motor to rotate the impeller. Further, the motor is capable of converting current into mechanical work by following the principle of Lorentz Law which states that, the current carrying conduction when placed in magnetic or electrical field experiences a force known as Lorentz force. Such that the motor converts the electrical current derived from an external source into a mechanical torque for providing the required rotational power to the impeller. The impeller vanes are designed in such a way that on rotation the impeller creates the negative pressure in the vacuum unit for extracting of welding fumes generated during welding. 

[0034] Moreover, the user accesses the display unit 110 to give input for moving the base 101 on the ground surface as per requirement based on that the microcontroller actuates multiple motorized omnidirectional wheels 102 provided underneath the base 101 to move the base 101. Each of the wheels 102 are coupled with a motor that is activated by the microcontroller to provide circular motion to the wheels 102 for moving the base 101 on the ground surface as per requirement.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to an adjustable security device that is capable of allowing an only authorized user to enter in an enclosure by means of verifying the biometric identity of the user, thus preventing unauthorized user to enter in the enclosure. Moreover, the device is also capable of being adjusted in accordance with the height of the user for allowing the user to input biometric impression before entering in the enclosure.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002]  An security device is a tool designed to enhance security by allowing customization to fit different needs or environments. Unlike fixed security solutions, these devices offer flexibility in their settings, such as adjustable locks, alarms, or surveillance features. This adaptability makes them suitable for a variety of applications, from home security to commercial use. Advantages include improved adaptability to changing security requirements, ease of upgrading or modifying features, and cost-effectiveness by reducing the need for multiple specialized devices. Overall, security devices provide a tailored approach to safeguarding assets and properties.

[0003]  Traditional biometric authentication methods include fingerprint recognition, iris scans, and facial recognition. These techniques rely on unique physical characteristics to verify identity. However, they have several drawbacks. Fingerprint scanners are affected by dirt or damage, and iris scans may be hindered by eye conditions or lighting. Facial recognition struggle with changes in appearance or lighting conditions and may raise privacy concerns. Additionally, these methods are vulnerable to spoofing or spoofed biometrics, where fake attributes are used to gain unauthorized access. Overall, while effective, traditional methods face challenges in accuracy, reliability, and security.

[0004] US6125192A discloses about an invention which includes fingerprint recognition system, comprise of a method and apparatus for fingerprint recognition is provided. A fingerprint is detected on a sensor. The fingerprint is digitized. A digitized background is subtracted from the fingerprint, resulting in a difference print. The difference print is matched with a database of fingerprint templates. Although US’192 relates to a device for fingerprint recognition, however, the cited prior art lacks in of adjusting the height of the biometric scanner as per the height of the user.

[0005] US20030141959A discloses about an invention which includes fingerprint biometric lock, comprises of a fingerprint biometric lock is provided which includes a locking mechanism that restricts the movement of an object that is to be unlocked, a movement restriction electronic circuit that restricts the unlocking of the object by the locking mechanism, a fingerprint sensor that detects a fingerprint pattern, a memory device that stores an enrolled fingerprint code data, a verifying unit that determines whether an offered fingerprint code, created from the fingerprint pattern sensed by the sensor, matches with any of the enrolled fingerprint codes stored in the memory device, a motor control unit that unlocks the locking mechanism through the movement restricting electronic circuit, when the offered and enrolled fingerprint codes match, and, a finger presence detector for powering a direct current to the sensor and the motor control unit. Although US’959 relates to a device for fingerprint biometric lock, however, the cited prior art lacks in storing the images of unauthorized person as the person’s fingerprint in not stored in the database.

[0006] Conventionally, many devices have been developed, however, these devices are incapable of adjusting the height of the biometric scanner as per the height of the user. Moreover, these devices are incapable of storing the images of unauthorize person as the person’s fingerprint in not stored in the database.

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of adjusting the height of the biometric scanner as per the user’s height. Furthermore, the device is capable to capture images of the user who is not the part of the organization for the future, if in case any investigation take place.

[0022]  Referring to Figure 1, an isometric view of adjustable security device illustrates as, a vertical elongated plate 101 developed to be fixed on a wall, an artificial intelligence based imaging unit 102 installed on the plate 101, a motorized slider 103 arranged on the plate 101, a cuboidal body 104 positioned on the slider 103 upward/downward, a finger scanner 105 configured in the body 104, a LED 106 light configured on the body 104, a display panel 107 installed on the body 104, a buzzer 108 housed in the body 104.

[0023]  The device includes a vertical elongated plate 101 designed for mounting on wall adjacent to the door of an enclosure. The plate 101 serves as the interface for the user to initiate the authentication process. The plate 101 is integrated with a push button which is strategically positioned for easy access by user. Upon pressing of the button, the circuits get closed allowing conduction of electricity that leads to activation of the device and vice versa. After switching on the device by the user, the microcontroller generates a command to actuate the security device.

[0024]  The device is equipped with an inbuilt microcontroller that is directly linked to the push button integrated into the vertical elongated plate 101. Upon activation by the user, this microcontroller triggers an artificial intelligence-based imaging unit 102, which includes a processor, also installed on the plate 101. The imaging unit 102 captures and processes images of the user standing in front of the device, specifically to determine the user's height. The imaging unit 102 comprises of an image capturing arrangement including a set of lenses that captures multiple images of the user present in front of the device and the captured images are stored within memory of the imaging unit 102 in form of an optical data. The imaging unit 102 also comprises of a processor that is integrated with artificial intelligence protocols, such that the processor processes the optical data and extracts the required data from the captured images. The extracted data is further converted into digital pulses and bits and are further transmitted to the microcontroller. The microcontroller processes the received data and determines height of the user standing Infront of the device. 

[0025]  Once the height is determined, the microcontroller actuates a motorized slider 103 mechanism that is arranged on the plate 101. This slider 103 is responsible for moving a cuboidal body 104, which is positioned on the slider 103, either upward or downward. The cuboidal body 104 is made up of any material but not limited to plastic, metal alike material. The motorized slider 103 typically consists of a motorized carriage attached to a rail, which enables controlled linear movement of the links along with a bar towards the sides of the plate 101. Upon actuation by the microcontroller, the motor drives the carriage along the rail, facilitating smooth and precise sliding motion of the cuboidal body 104 along with the bar towards the side of the plate 101. 

[0026]  The device features a fingerprint scanner integrated within the cuboidal body 104 positioned on the motorized slider 103. The finger scanner 105 is configured to be easily accessed by the user, allowing them to provide their fingerprint impressions. These impressions are then compared against a plurality of pre-stored fingerprint patterns stored in a database linked to the microcontroller. Upon a successful match between the user's fingerprint impression and the pre-stored patterns, the microcontroller triggers an LED 106 (light-emitting diode) light, also configured on the cuboidal body 104, to emit a green light. The LED 106 is a two-lead semiconductor light source also known as p-n junction which produce the lighting when constant voltage is supplied across the diode. When the voltage is supplied across the diode, the electrons recombine with the electrons hole in the diode which result in conversion of electron into photons which is another form of light.

[0027] This green illumination serves as a visual notification to the user, indicating that authentication has been successful. Following the successful authentication, the microcontroller generates a corresponding command to initiate the opening of the door to the enclosure, thereby granting the user entry or exit from the secured area.

[0028] The body 104 have a feature to handle unsuccessful authentication attempts. In such cases, the microcontroller activates the LED 106 light, which is integrated into the body 104, to emit a red light. The red illumination serves as an immediate visual indicator of the failed authentication. Following this, the microcontroller triggers a buzzer 108, also housed within the body 104, to emit an alerting sound. The buzzer 108's sound is designed to notify concerned individuals or security personnel of the unauthorized attempt to access the enclosure. This dual alert device combining both visual and audible cues ensures that any unauthorized access attempt is promptly and effectively communicated, thereby enhancing the overall security provided by the device.

[0029] Upon unsuccessful authentication is detected, the microcontroller triggers the imaging unit 102, which is integrated into the device, to capture images of the user. These images are then stored in the device's database, which is linked to the microcontroller. The captured images provide a visual record of the individual attempting unauthorized access, allowing for further investigation and review by security personnel. The feature enhances the security capabilities of the device by not only deterring unauthorized access but also by creating a documented trail that is used for subsequent analysis and identification.

[0030] The scanner is fabricated with a temperature sensor which is based on infrared. The sensor is designed to measure the user's body 104 temperature during their interaction with the device. As the user places their finger on the scanner for authentication, the infrared sensor simultaneously records the temperature. The recorded temperature is then transmitted to the microcontroller, which displays the temperature reading on a display panel 107 installed on the body 104. The functionality not only provides an additional layer of health monitoring but also integrates seamlessly into the user authentication process, ensuring that the device tracks and display critical information in real-time.

[0031] A timer module is responsible for accurately recording the exact time of the user’s entrance and exit from the enclosure. The timer module is integrated with the microcontroller. When the user interacts with the device by pressing the push button and undergoing fingerprint authentication, the timer module automatically records the time at which these actions occur. The precise time-stamping function is crucial for logging the user’s activity, ensuring that the device maintains an accurate record of entry and exit times. The integration of the timer module into the microcontroller allows for seamless operation, enabling the device to efficiently track and document the timing of user interactions without requiring any additional user input.

[0032]  A display panel 107 installed on the cuboidal body 104 positioned on the motorized slider 103. This display panel 107 is activated by the microcontroller upon successful authentication. The panel serves multiple functions, including displaying the user's identification (ID) and the exact time of their entrance or exit from the enclosure. Additionally, the display panel 107 shows the status of the user, indicating whether they are late or have entered on time. This real-time feedback provided by the display panel 107 ensures that users are immediately informed of their entry status, adding an additional layer of convenience and security to the device.

[0033] The body 104 is integrated with a chamber, which is paired with a nozzle situated near the fingerprint scanner. The chamber is made up of any material but not limited to plastic and metal alike material. The chamber is connected to the nozzle by means of a conduit, allowing the flow of a sanitizing solution. After the user's attendance is recorded, the microcontroller activates a speaker installed on the body 104. This speaker generates audible instructions, notifying the user to remove their finger from the scanner. Following this, the microcontroller actuates the nozzle to spray the sanitizing solution stored in the chamber onto the fingerprint scanner. This process ensures that the scanner is sanitized after each use, thereby maintaining hygiene and reducing the risk of contamination.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to an automated mortar mixture molding device that is capable of molding and levelling the mortar mixture over a boundary by regulating the shape as per the curvature of the boundary in order to shape the mortar according to user desired thickness. 

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002]  Mortar mixing and molding devices are essential tools in construction for preparing and applying mortar, a key material in masonry and plastering. These devices include portable mixers that blend cement, sand, and water to the desired consistency, ensuring uniformity and quality of mortar. Molding devices like trowels and floats are used to apply and smooth mortar onto surfaces, ensuring proper adhesion and finish. They facilitate efficient construction processes, reducing labor intensity and improving workmanship. Advances in technology have led to electric and pneumatic mortar mixers, enhancing productivity and precision in mixing operations, crucial for modern construction projects. 

[0003]  Traditional methods of mortar mixing involve manual labor using shovels or hoes to blend cement, sand, and water on a flat surface. Molding is typically done by hand with trowels or wooden floats to apply and smooth mortar on walls or surfaces. Drawbacks include inconsistent mixing ratios, leading to variations in mortar quality. Manual mixing is labor-intensive and time-consuming, affecting productivity. Hand molding can result in uneven application and finishing, impacting structural integrity and aesthetics. Moreover, traditional methods may not meet modern construction standards for consistency, strength, and durability, necessitating advancements in mechanized mixing and molding technologies. 

[0004] WO1990009875A1 discloses horizontally oriented mortar mixing drum fabricated of polyethylene material having an elemental cylindrical segment opening through which mortar materials to be mixed may be deposited into or poured from. A perimeter frame having base elemental frame member, diametric wall frame members and polyethylene grate is provided for enhancing resistance to torsional stress on drum. Wear resistant liner and side panels and cover the interior surface of drum. Paddle shaft is rotatable and axially supported within drum and has paddle stubs attached to and extending radially therefrom. Polyethylene mixing paddles are sleeved onto paddle stubs to complete improved mortar mixing drum assembly. Although WO’875 relates to an improved mortar mixing drum, and in particular to a mortar mixing drum fabricated from polyethylene crosslink with a removable wear resistant plastic liner and paddles, and an elemental perimeter drum frame for rigidity. However the cited prior art lacks in providing assistive means for levelling and molding the mortar mixture over the boundary in an effective manner without manual efforts of the user. 

[0005] US3799714A discloses a portable device for applying mortar to desired portions of successive courses of block, brick, or any flat surface to improve the construction of masonry walls. The device includes a hopper, vibrator, and a base assembly having side guides for drawing the applicator along a course of block and dispensing mortar for laying the next course. Though US’714 relates to art of mortar applicators and, more particularly, to an apparatus for applying a layer of mortar to substantially any desired surface. However the cited prior art lacks in providing assistive means for levelling and molding the mortar mixture over the boundary in an effective manner without manual efforts of the user. 
 
[0006] Conventionally, many devices have been developed that are capable of molding the mortar mixture but no such device exists and have been developed that is efficient enough to mold and level the mortar mixture over the boundary by regulating the shape as the curvature of the boundary. 

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of molding and levelling the mortar mixture over a boundary by regulating the shape as per the curvature of the boundary in order to shape the mortar according to user desired thickness.

[0008]  The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]  An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of molding and levelling the boundary of building with mortar mixture in an effective manner. 

[0010] Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of levelling the mortar mixture as per user desired thickness. 

[0011]  Yet another object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of mitigating the time and efforts employed by the user while molding and levelling the mortar over the boundary.

[0013]  The present invention relates to an automated mortar mixture molding device that is capable of effectively molding and levelling the mortar mixture as per user desired thickness over a boundary. 

[0014]  According to an embodiment of the present invention, an automated mortar mixture molding device comprising of an inverted L-shaped plate positioned over a boundary along which mortar mixture is to be molded, touch interactive display panel installed over the plate to enable a user to provide input regarding thickness of the mortar mixture to be molded, a multi-sectioned container arranged with the plate and stored with cement, sand, aggregates and water, an electronic valve installed with each section of the container dispense a regulated amount of the cement, sand, aggregates and water within the chamber connected with the valves, a motorized stirrer installed in the chamber mix the received cement, sand, aggregates and water in order to make the mortar mixture, an inverted L-shaped telescopic rod installed over top portion of the plate extend and position a flap configured with the rod at a specific distance in accordance with the user-specified thickness as monitored via an ultrasonic senor installed with the flap, a pair of motorized grippers installed with the plate each by means of an inverted L-shaped telescopic bar extend and grip the boundary via the grippers in a secured manner to provide stability to the plate over the boundary, an artificial intelligence based imaging unit installed over the plate and integrated with a laser measurement sensor captures images of the boundary to determines curvature of the boundary, plurality of motorized hinge joints integrated in the flap to regulate shape of the flap in accordance with the detected curvature, a chamber stored with mortar mixture arranged with the plate.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to a safe and secured parcel collection assistive device that is capable of collecting multiple parcels in a self-sufficient manner by authenticating parcel delivery individual and accordingly allows the individual to access a storage for accommodating parcel securely.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002]  Parcel collection is a critical service in modern logistics, driven by the growing demands of e-commerce and global trade. As online shopping continues to surge, consumers increasingly seek convenient and flexible options for receiving their purchases. Parcel collection services address this need by offering designated locations where customers can pick up their packages at their convenience, rather than waiting for home delivery. This system alleviates issues such as missed deliveries and provides a solution for those who may not be available during traditional delivery windows. Furthermore, parcel collection points, such as lockers or retail partners, often streamline the logistics chain, reducing the burden on delivery drivers and minimizing the environmental impact associated with multiple delivery attempts. The rise of urbanization and the corresponding pressure on delivery infrastructure also necessitate efficient parcel collection solutions to manage the volume of shipments and avoid congestion. In essence, parcel collection is a response to the evolving needs of consumers and the logistical challenges faced by delivery networks, offering a practical and efficient approach to modern parcel management.

[0003] Parcel collection equipment includes a range of technologies designed to facilitate the efficient retrieval of packages. Parcel lockers, which are automated systems allowing customers to pick up parcels at their convenience from secure, self-service kiosks. These lockers are typically found in high-traffic areas such as shopping centers or transit stations. Another important piece of equipment is the parcel collection point, often located in retail stores or convenience shops, where customers can retrieve their packages during regular business hours. Additionally, some systems utilize smart locker technology with integrated sensors and digital interfaces for enhanced user experience. However, each of these solutions has drawbacks. Parcel lockers, while convenient, require significant initial investment and maintenance costs. They also face limitations in capacity and can be susceptible to vandalism or theft. Collection points in retail stores might lead to longer wait times during peak hours and can cause additional foot traffic for the retailers.
 
[0004] US2006169762A1 discloses an apparatus for receiving parcels having a structural frame and a parcel drop having a fully open and a fully closed position is disclosed. The apparatus includes a bin, a first opening between the bin and the structural frame through which patrons may deposit parcels into the bin at least when the parcel drop is in the fully open position. The apparatus further includes a second opening within the bin through which deposited parcels may fall out of the bin at least when the parcel drop is in the fully closed position. The parcel drop is rotatably coupled to the structural frame. Although US’762 relates to a parcel collection device and method, however, the cited art has limitation in eliminating chances of causing damage to the parcel by handling multiple parcels securely.

[0005] JP2828060B2 discloses a problem to be solved: To attain a package collection/delivery system capable of completely managing information from the collection of packages up to the completion of delivery at real time. Solution: When a sender executes operation for sending a package by a package collection part arranged in each place, the information is sent to a collection/delivery information management part in a collection/delivery information center through a line network and the package is accepted. A transport means transports the collected package to a package distribution center, sorted and delivered to a delivery destination by a transport means. At the time of delivery, an information I/O part reads out a bar code from each package at each point of time and sends the read information to the management part. Thus, the current state of each package can be managed at real time from its reception. Though JP’060 relates to a package collection and delivery system, however, the cited art has limitation in collecting parcel in an automated manner from an authenticated parcel delivery individual.
 
[0006] Conventionally, many devices have been developed for parcel delivery, however the devices mentioned in the prior arts have limitations pertaining to collect parcel by authenticating parcel delivery individual in a self-sufficient manner.

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of authenticating parcel delivery individual for delivery of parcel and accordingly accommodates a parcel safe and securely.

A Battery Management System (BMS) is an essential component for managing the performance, safety, and longevity of rechargeable battery packs. The need for BMS technology has grown significantly in recent years due to the widespread adoption of energy storage solutions, particularly in electric vehicles (EVs), renewable energy systems, and portable electronics. The growing demand for reliable, efficient, and safe battery usage across various industries makes BMS a critical area of technological development

The development of efficient energy storage systems plays a pivotal role in the transition to cleaner energy sources and sustainable power solutions. As renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power become more mainstream, the demand for high-performance energy storage systems has increased. This has led to a surge in the adoption of Lithium-ion (Li-ion) and other advanced battery technologies, which are susceptible to issues like overcharging,


over-discharging, temperature fluctuations, and aging-related degradation. To ensure the safe and reliable operation of these batteries, an effective Battery Management System (BMS) is 
required.
A BMS is responsible for monitoring and managing battery health, charge status, temperature, and overall system performance to extend battery life and optimize efficiency. It ensures that individual cells within the battery pack are balanced, preventing overcharging or overdischarging, which can lead to reduced lifespan or even catastrophic failure. Moreover, with growing concerns about battery-safety, the BMS also incorporates features to protect the battery pack from risks such as thermal runaway and short circuits.
In automotive applications, such as electric vehicles (EVs), the BMS ensures the safe operation of High-voltage” battery packs. contfols=the charging and discharging-cycles^ and maintains cell voltage balance. In stationary energy storage systems, the BMS helps optimize charge/discharge cycles and monitors the health of the cells to ensure consistent energy supply and minimize costly replacements.
With the rapid advancements in battery technology and the increased complexity of modern battery systems, the design of a highly efficient and intelligent BMS has become critical. It integrates hardware and software components to continuously monitor and evaluate the performance of the battery cells in real-time. By doing so, it not only helps optimize battery life but also enables predictive maintenance and enhances the safety features of battery- powered devices.
The challenges in designing a BMS are compounded by the need for low-power operation, high scalability, and integration with other system components. The growing emphasis on smart grid technology, the Internet of Things (IoT), and the integration of battery storage with renewable energy sources requires that BMS solutions evolve to become more adaptive and 
intelligent.


Summary of this Invention The Battery Management System (BMS) described in this invention provides an innovative solution to the challenges of monitoring, managing, and optimizing the performance and safety of rechargeable battery packs in various applications. The system incorporates a combination of hardware and software components to monitor critical parameters such as battery voltage, temperature, state of charge (SOC), state of health (SOH), and individual cell balancing, ensuring optimal performance throughout the battery's life cycle.
The invention focuses on enhancing the efficiency, safety, and longevity of the battery by incorporating a variety of features that address the key issues of overcharging, over­discharging, thermal management, and cell balancing. By providing real-time data and control over these parameters, the BMS ensures that the battery operates within safe limits, thus preventing failures that could result in reduced battery performance, safety hazards, or even catastrophic events such as fire or explosion.
The system is designed with intelligent monitoring capabilities that continuously assess the health of the battery and predict future performance based on real-time data analytics. This predictive maintenance approach helps identify potential issues before they lead to-failure, enabling timely interventions and reducing the likelihood of unplanned downtimes.
In this invention, the battery cell balancing technology has been enhanced to provide more accurate charge distribution across individual cells. This feature ensures that each cell in the battery pack operates at an optimal state, reducing the risk of one cell becoming overcharged or over-discharged, which can shorten the overall life of the battery pack.
The thermal management system integrated into the BMS is another key innovation. The BMS employs sensors to monitor the temperature of the battery cells and adjusts the charge/discharge rate accordingly to prevent overheating. Overheating is a major cause of reduced battery lifespan and, in extreme cases, can lead to thermal runaway, which can be catastrophic. This invention also includes an advanced cooling mechanism that actively manages the temperature of the battery pack in high-performance environments, such as electric vehicles or high-capacity energy storage systems.
The system’s modular architecture allows for scalability, making it suitable for a wide range of applications, from small portable electronics to large-scale energy storage systems and electric vehicles. The BMS can be easily integrated with existing battery technologies, and its 

modular nature allows for easy upgrades or expansion, ensuring that the system remains adaptable to future advancements in battery technology.
The user interface of the BMS provides clear and actionable insights into the battery’s performance, with real-time monitoring capabilities and alerts for any abnormalities. 
Additionally, the system can be integrated into larger networked infrastructures, allowing for remote monitoring and control, which is especially useful in large-scale commercial or industrial applications.
Detailed Description of this Invention The Battery Management System (BMS) according to this invention provides a highly efficient and scalable solution for monitoring, managing, and optimizing rechargeable battery packs, particularly in high-performance and safety-critical applications, such as electric vehicles, renewable energy storage, and portable electronics.
The BMS operates through a combination of hardware components and software algorithms. 
The hardware consists of a series of sensors, microcontrollers, communication interfaces, and power management units. These components work together to monitor and control various parameters of the battery pack, including individual cell voltage, temperature, current, and state of charge (SOC). The BMS is capable of monitoring each individual cell within the battery pack, ensuring that all cells are balanced and operate within safe parameters.
The core components of the BMS include:
Voltage Monitoring: The system continuously monitors the voltage of each individual battery cell to ensure that they are within the specified range. Over-voltage or under-voltage conditions are detected; and corrective actions are taken to prevent damage to the cells.
State of Charge (SOC) Calculation: The BMS uses algorithms to calculate the state of charge (SOC) of the battery pack. This allows the system to determine how much energy is remaining in the battery and when a recharge is required.

State of Health (SOH) Monitoring: The system calculates the state of health (SOH) of the battery by assessing factors such as capacity degradation, cycle life, and internal resistance. 
This allows for predictive maintenance and early detection of performance degradation.
Cell Balancing: An advanced cell balancing mechanism is employed to ensure that all cells in the battery pack are at the same voltage level. This helps prevent certain cells from being overcharged or over-discharged, thus ensuring a longer lifespan for the battery pack.
Temperature Monitoring and Thermal Management: The BMS incorporates multiple temperature sensors to monitor the temperature of the battery pack. If the temperature exceeds a threshold, the system can reduce the charging/discharging rate or activate cooling mechanisms (e.g., fans or liquid cooling systems) to maintain safe operating conditions.
Current Monitoring: The system measures the current flowing into and out of the battery pack to prevent over-current conditions that could damage the battery cells. The BMS adjusts charging or discharging operations based on the current levels.
Communication Interface: The BMS features a communication interface for integration with other systems. This could include vehicle control units in electric vehicles or supervisory systems in large-scale energy storage systems. The BMS communicates real-time data about battery performance, alerts, and maintenance recommendations to these systems.
The software algorithms in the BMS enable intelligent decision-making by analyzing the collected data in real-time. The system’s firmware uses predictive models to forecast the remaining battery life, detect early signs of failure, and optimize charging/discharging cycles. 
The software is capable of adjusting parameters dynamically based on changing environmental conditions or battery usage patterns.
In high-performance applications, such as electric vehicles, the BMS can interface with the vehicle’s energy management system to optimize performance. It ensures that the battery operates at the highest efficiency while protecting it from conditions that could lead to overheating or premature failure.


The system’s user interface provides real-time feedback to users regarding battery status, including SOC, SOH, temperature, and performance alerts. The interface can be integrated with mobile apps or cloud-based platforms for remote monitoring, making it ideal for large- scale deployments in commercial and industrial sectors.

Remote monitoring of vehicle health allows for proactive maintenance, reduces the risk of unexpected breakdowns, and enhances overall vehicle reliability and safety.

Example 3: Induction of the Alzheimer diabetic animal model

After the adaptive feeding of 60 rats for 2 days, 12 rats were fed with basic feed without any treatment as a vehicle control (Normal). The remaining 48 rats were organized into 4 groups, each consisting of 12 individuals, as detailed below: Alzheimer diabetic rats without any drug treatment (Disease control group); Alzheimer diabetic rats treated with Glimepiride (10 mg/kg) and Donepezil (1 mg/kg) (served as a standard control group); and Alzheimer diabetic rats treated with Imatinib  composition of present invention at doses of 1 & 5 mg/kg  (test treatment groups 1 & 2). Alzheimer diabetic rats had been induced with STZ 35 mg/kg i.p in combination with a bilateral hippocampal injection of 7.5 µL of Aß25–35.
Initially, the diabetic rat model was established. Rats in the disease control group, all test treatment groups, and the standard control group were fed a high-fat diet for 4 weeks. On the last day of the 4th week, rats in each group began fasting, excluding water, at 5:00 PM, 1 day before the injection of STZ. At 9:00 am the next day, rats were injected with STZ (35 mg/kg b.w.) dissolved in freshly prepared 0.1 mol/L sodium citrate buffer (pH 4.4). After 72 h, fasting blood glucose (FBG) was measured by a portable glucometer from the tail vein. Rats with FBG levels of 11.1 mmol/L or higher were considered as a successfully induced diabetic model and were used in subsequent experiments.
Subsequently, the Alzheimer diabetic rat model was established. Seven days later, all diabetic rats were anesthetized with Ketamine (75mg/kg) in combination with Xylazine (25mg/kg) and fixed on a brain stereotaxic instrument. Two holes were drilled by a dental auger after defined points stereotaxically, specifically two points in bilateral hippocampal areas (behind the bregma 4.4 mm, meta 2.2 mm, deep 3.0 mm). The left hippocampus was localized first, followed by the right hippocampus. Rats were injected with Aß25–35 at 7.5 µL on each side. The escape latency in the Morris water maze and passive avoidance test were then evaluated to indicate the successful establishment of the Alzheimer diabetic rat model compared with the vehicle control group.
Disease control rats were treated with Imatinib composition and Glimepiride (10 mg/kg) and Donepezil (1 mg/kg) for 28 days, respectively. During the same period, disease control group rats were fed a high-fat diet without drug treatment, and vehicle control rats were fed basic feed without any intervention, for a total of 28 days.

Description:DETAILED DESCRIPTION   
[0013] This disclosure provides a composition for managing urolithiasis, which may include a papaya peel extract (PAPE) standardized with respect to total phenol content (TPC) and total flavonoid content (TFC).  Papaya peel extract (PAPE) is derived from the outer skin of the papaya fruit (Carica papaya), which is known for its rich phytochemical profile. Papaya peels are abundant in bioactive compounds such as phenols, flavonoids, alkaloids, and enzymes like papain. These compounds exhibit a wide range of pharmacological properties, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities, which make papaya peel extract a valuable candidate for therapeutic applications. One of its promising applications is in the management of urolithiasis, a condition characterized by the formation of calcium oxalate (CaOx) kidney stones. The bioactive compounds in papaya peel extract work synergistically to inhibit calcium oxalate crystal formation by interfering with the nucleation, aggregation, and growth of crystals. Additionally, its antioxidant properties help mitigate oxidative stress, which plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of kidney stone formation. The extract also provides a safer alternative to conventional chemical treatments by minimizing potential side effects through its natural composition.
[0014] The preparation of papaya peel extract involves a series of carefully controlled steps to ensure its bioactive composition is preserved and standardized. Fresh papaya peels are collected, thoroughly washed under running water to remove dirt and contaminants, and allowed to air dry. The cleaned peels are dried in a shaded area at room temperature or in a hot air oven at a controlled temperature of 40–50°C to prevent the degradation of heat-sensitive compounds. Once completely dried, the peels are ground into a fine powder using a grinder or milling machine. The powdered form allows for efficient extraction of bioactive compounds. The powdered peels are subjected to extraction using a suitable solvent such as ethanol, water, or a hydroalcoholic mixture (30:70 ethanol:water) in a ratio of 1:10 (powder:solvent). The mixture is stirred continuously or macerated for 24–48 hours to extract phenolic and flavonoid compounds effectively.
[0015] The extract is filtered through a muslin cloth or filter paper to remove solid residues, leaving a filtrate that contains the soluble bioactive compounds. The filtrate is concentrated using a rotary evaporator or by gentle heating under reduced pressure to remove excess solvent and obtain a concentrated extract. The concentrated extract is standardized by measuring its total phenol content (TPC) and total flavonoid content (TFC) using spectrophotometric methods. This ensures consistency and accuracy in its bioactive composition across different batches. The standardized extract is stored in sterile, airtight containers at a temperature of 4–8°C to preserve its stability and potency. The prepared extract is evaluated against calcium oxalate (CaOx) crystal formation using nucleation, aggregation, growth, and dissolution assays. These evaluations confirm its ability to inhibit crystal formation and growth, making it a viable therapeutic agent for managing urolithiasis. By following this systematic preparation process, papaya peel extract is developed into a reliable, effective, and standardized formulation for therapeutic use in conditions like urolithiasis.
[0016] In an extension of this, the present invention also provides liquid composition of papaya peel extract (PAPE) wherein the PAPE can be present at a concentration range of 80-100 mg/mL and may be combined with pharmaceutically acceptable excipients such as distilled water, glycerin, citric acid, ascorbic acid, potassium sorbate, sodium benzoate, honey, stevia, polysorbate 80, and a pH adjuster. The composition can be adjusted to a pH range of 5.5 to 6.5 for compatibility with human use. The PAPE may be evaluated against calcium oxalate (CaOx) crystal formation using assays like nucleation, aggregation, growth, and dissolution assays to determine its efficacy in inhibiting CaOx crystal formation. The composition can be administered to subjects in need of managing urolithiasis, offering a potential alternative therapy with synergistic and side-effect neutralizing effects. The preparation of PAPE involves phytochemical analysis and standardization to ensure consistency and accuracy in its bioactive composition, which may contribute to its effectiveness as a therapeutic agent.

The PAPE may be used as an active ingredient, solvent base, solubilizer, stabilizer, preservative, flavoring agent, solubilizer for hydrophobic bioactives, and pH adjuster. The extract may be phytochemically analyzed and prepared to inhibit calcium oxalate crystal formation. [0018] The composition for managing urolithiasis incorporates a variety of pharmaceutically acceptable excipients, each selected for its specific role in ensuring stability, solubility, and compatibility. Examples of solvents include distilled water and purified water, which provide a base for dissolving the active ingredient. Solubilizers and viscosity enhancers such as glycerin and propylene glycol ensure uniform distribution and improve texture. Stabilizers like citric acid and ascorbic acid prevent oxidation and maintain the integrity of bioactive compounds. Preservatives such as potassium sorbate and sodium benzoate inhibit microbial growth, extending the shelf life of the composition. Abstract:
Abstract:

A composition for masking the unpleasant taste of bitter medications includes a thin, fast-dissolving oral film and miraculin, a taste-modifying protein derived from Synsepalum dulcificum fruit. When dissolved in the oral cavity, miraculin binds to human taste receptors, altering the perception of bitter substances to taste sweet. The oral film is produced using a solvent casting method, involving dissolving a biopolymer and miraculin in a suitable solvent, casting the solution onto a flat surface, and allowing the solvent to evaporate. The composition may include additives such as plasticizers, stabilizers, and preservatives, and is suitable for pediatric and geriatric patients, as well as those with chronic conditions requiring long-term treatment with bitter medications. It is packaged in moisture-proof packaging to maintain its form and functionality.

[0043] The preparation of miraculin-infused oral films involves a systematic process using the solvent casting method, ensuring a uniform and efficient formulation. Initially, the selected biopolymer, such as hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) or polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), is dissolved in a suitable solvent like water or ethanol to form a homogeneous film-forming solution. This step ensures the creation of a consistent base for the film. Subsequently, miraculin, the active taste-modifying protein derived from Synsepalum dulcificum, is carefully incorporated into the solution at concentrations ranging from 0.5% to 5% w/w. Additional components, including plasticizers like glycerol or propylene glycol (0.1% to 10% w/w), stabilizers such as sorbitol or mannitol (0.05% to 1% w/w), and preservatives like potassium sorbate or sodium benzoate (0.05% to 1% w/w), are added to enhance the film's flexibility, stability, and shelf life.

[0044] The resulting solution is mixed thoroughly to ensure even distribution of all components. This mixture is then cast onto a flat, non-stick surface or casting plate using a controlled applicator to achieve the desired thickness. The cast solution is subjected to a drying process under controlled temperature conditions to allow solvent evaporation, leading to the formation of a thin, flexible film. Once dried, the film is carefully peeled off the casting surface and trimmed into uniform strips of appropriate size.
